A look back at Killer Kross's destructive run in IMPACT Wrestling.
Gold fever takes hold when Nellie learns that nuggets just lay on the ground in a remote area of Mexico.
Police and Elly's animals converge on the Clampett estate when Pearl starts giving yodeling lessons.
Two of Cousin Pearl's most ardent former suitors come to visit her in Beverly Hills; Jed doesn't know what to suggest.
Granny's plan to stop Pearl's yodeling backfires when the police she called find her illegal still.
Jed's bloodhound Duke takes on the role of matchmaker for his master and a glamorous woman from France.
A confidence man tries to sell Jed the Hollywood Bowl, Griffith Park and the Hollywood Freeway.
An authority on American history finds evidence that Jed's ancestors preceded the Mayflower to America.
Cousin Pearl gets a glamour treatment and tries to groom the Clampetts for high society.
Jed takes a dose of Granny's tonic and ends up on Lovers Lane with a gold-digging secretary.
A Navy officer mapping the Missouri River encounters a struggle between Indians and the Army.
A miner gets tricked into selling his claim on a gold mine.
Pegarski is mistreated by mine manager Short because of a rivalry over Mary Parker; a cave-in alters the situation as Mary holds vigil for a loved one.
A former prospector agrees to search the mountains for a woman's missing fiancé.
A kidnapper who delivers unwilling brides to a religious cult realizes his shame.
Teacher Ruth Stewart suspects a gambler stole money meant for a new school and tries to win it back.
A father who raised a cold-hearted killer worries his younger son may turn out the same way.
A vagabond finds stolen riches and becomes a philanthropist.
A female patriot meets a man helping an invasion of Mexico.
A reformed criminal's former partners in crime come calling after robbing a bank.
Indians attack on the night of a rancher's wedding.
Pearl's attempts to snag Mr. Brewster seem hopeless until he suddenly makes an outrageous public proposal.
Jed is confronted with too many cooks and not enough vittles when he invites Pearl and Jethrine to Beverly Hills.
Trying to cool a feud between Granny and Pearl, Jed takes his family on a sightseeing tour of Beverly Hills.
An IRS agent calls on the Clampetts and gets a roaring shotgun welcome from Granny.
Little Joe falls for a girl who has been disowned by her people because they think she is a witch and, therefore, an outcast.
A member of a powerful gang murders a shopkeeper; the deputized Cartwrights sentence a murderer to hang at dawn when the leader of the gang kidnaps Ben and holds him hostage.
When a cook skims gold nuggets off miners while working at their camp, his assistant reaches out to his sister from Tucson in an attempt to save him from hanging.
Lumberjack Will is attracted to Trudy, the daughter of his boss Mr. Bell; Trudy thinks highly of herself and Will refuses to indulge her spoiled, pampered ways.
A rich miner seeks to buy out his competitors.
Teens and an alcoholic ex-wrestler come up against street toughs who want to run them out of their gathering place.

Herman Broder (Ron Silver), a Holocaust survivor living in New York City and struggling with depression after his ordeals in the war, makes his living ghostwriting for a rabbi. Herman is married to Yadwiga (Margaret Sophie Stein) but is also having an affair with Masha (Lena Olin), a married woman. Things grow even more chaotic when Herman's first wife, Tamara (Anjelica Huston), who he thought had died in the war, shows up in New York as well. Based on the novel by Isaac Bashevis Singer.
A woman repeatedly remarries after repeatedly marrying the wrong guy; a man is put on trial for sexually harassing himself; the hip guy and his wife introduce their lovers.
A man has to get back up on a horse after choking on a chicken kabob; cops talk about what they might have done if they hadn't become cops; Buddy searches for a new lover.
A man who works in a wig shop tries to convince everyone he's not bald; a pizza guy lusts after schoolgirls; Sid wonders if he is too small to love.
Poems by the Emperor of Japan; Brice's advice for breaking into showbiz.
A businessman just stares; a man debates whether he should call a girl; the cops wonder why someone would abandon a perfectly good potato.
Mississippi Gary sings the After-Death blues; the Fact Girl discusses the importance of cleaning the ears; one of the Sizzler Sisters becomes sane.
A man reminisces about the Flying Pig; a woman names her god; Tanya annoys people at a party.
The alternate conclusion to "Old Yeller"; drugs and other vices; how to deal with noisy people.
Celebrating Scott's 100th portrayal of a waiter; Hecubus is fired and rehired; a wife walks in on her husband and a thief in bed.
Hank believes he can run a gumball business, but Oscar lends his help and a hidden talent from Karen helps it succeed.
Brents finds a way to stop Oscar from saying the J-word, but discovers it might not have been so bad.
Hank and Davis lead the fight against a call center that might come to Dog River.
Lacey is suspicious of the illegal duplication of Dog River money; Hank gets a case of pink eye, causing Brent and Wanda to panic in Corner Gas; Karen is frustrated with Davis.
Emma goes Christmas shopping early making everyone curious to find out what they are getting.
Lacey gets invited to join the Dog River Women's Club, but soon realizes that it isn't right for her.
Karen and Davis figure out a way to get Emma to do free cleaning.
Oscar and Emma discover an easy way to make some fast money; Davis decides to take off with Brent's car.
It's the eve of Brent's 40th birthday; to celebrate, the town has planned a midnight party complete with fireworks and a parade.
A cable guy visits Dog River to help produce some local access programming, but the town isn't quite ready for prime time; Brent is selected to choose which idea will be produced.
Jung shows Shannon his nurturing side while Chelsea and Gerald get in the way of Janet's summer plans; Appa is invited to lead a business seminar but is forced to share the spotlight.
Umma believes she has discovered a murder weapon, as Janet realizes she and Nathan have nothing in common; at Handy, Kimchee struggles to fit in with the other regional managers.
Appa and Umma's plans for the future push Appa out of his comfort zone; Janet gets an internship overseas, and Jung and Kimchee explore new living arrangements.
Umma's new parking pass gives Appa an idea; Janet searches for more meaningful work; Shannon's mix-up leads to an awkward situation for the Handy staff.
Appa destroys a piece of Gerald's childhood; Umma misrepresents herself to her support group; Shannon gets in the way of Kimchee's plan to visit Jung in California.
Umma and Appa try to fit in at an upscale tennis court; Shannon helps Omar deal with his over-eager family; Janet misjudges a co-worker.
Appa's nerves are tested when Nayoung arrives with a furry friend; Umma shares an uncomfortable lunch with Jung and Shannon; bad timing makes Kimchee neglect a co-worker in need.
Appa finds marijuana in the house; Shannon throws a staff party that doesn't go as planned.
Appa and Kimchee enjoy an impromptu hangout together; Janet and Umma find an envelope of money in the store; Jung and Shannon struggle to watch TV together.
Drunken driver attempts an ATM withdrawal at a drive-up police station; pilfering exterminator; unsolicited confession.
A dog leads cops to its pot possessing owners; a new tool for law enforcement; a thief gets a flood of trouble.
Marijuana farmer tries to claim his confiscated crop; robber battles change machine; shoplifter tries to sell merchandise.
Thief steals a policeman's truck and returns it along with his identification; hungry crook robs deli and makes sandwich.
An employee steals a car to be on time; jewel thief wears loot with tags; a man turns himself in for a reward.
One peeping Tom turns in another; drug dealer accepts patch explanation; drunken driver asks police for a room.
A bank robber uses his phone bill to light a fuse; incontinent burglar; parents ask for marijuana used as evidence in their son's trial.
Criminals try to enter a house through the chimney; cab driver; a man who should have called for a ride.
Emma and Karen look for a suitable gift to send their twin town in Japan; Wanda attempts to become the advice giving bartender.
Oscar is asked to be a school bus driver for the day; the kids may not be the only ones who need a lesson in good behavior.
Brent meets a new member of his extended family; Karen helps Wanda showcase her math skills; Ruby makes menu changes.
Oscar tries to catch a mouse; Brent and Hank invent a new game.
Lacey sets up an employee of the month program; Hank takes up a new hobby, and drives Emma crazy.
A boy (Julian Dennison) and his foster father (Sam Neill) become the subjects of a manhunt after they get stranded in the New Zealand wilderness.
A successful writer (Greg Kinnear) tries to reconnect with his two children (Lily Collins, Nat Wolff) after his divorce.
El retador es un chef obstinado que desciende de una larga línea de habitantes de Tokio. El Iron Chef tiene las manos llenas al enfrentarse a una tradición tan fuerte.
El retador es uno de los pocos especialistas en comida mexicana en Tokio. Se lleva a cabo un duelo latino en Kitchen Stadium.
André Pachón es el líder de la comunidad de chefs franceses en Japón, ya aparecieron varios de sus aprendices, pero esta vez Pachón envía a su hombre número 1.
El hermano menor de los hermanos Liang, soberanos de la cocina cantonesa en Japón, se enfrenta a Iron Chef Chinese.
Iron Chef Chen llama la atención del retador Lian Su Qin usando konnyaku, una comida saludable japonesa única.
El antiguo Iron Chef Michiba decide que Morimoto necesita ayuda para encontrar su camino, así que recluta a su sous chef número uno de sus propios días en el Estadio de la Cocina.
Los 14 chefs restantes reciben una lección sobre preparar sushi de Masaharu Morimoto de Iron Chef antes de hacerlo ellos mismos. Un competidor en particular parece que no tiene éxito.

Llega el reto de los ravioles, el premio es un viaje en helicóptero. Trev se siente menospreciado por su equipo. Melissa se confunde con los números, no puede sumar tres más tres en la noche italiana. Sabrina se altera y no puede dar los tiempos.
El chef Gordon Ramsay les pone un nuevo reto a los participantes, deben organizar el menú de un baile de graduación. Al final de la noche habrá un integrante eliminado.
El desafío de esta semana consiste en la creatividad de los competidores. Ramsay quiere llevarlos al límite y les pide que creen una ensalada innovadora.
Trabajando juntos, los concursantes deberán crear un plato cohesivo usando cinco ingredientes seleccionados al azar.
Los equipos participan en una prueba de sabor; Ramsay desafía a los equipos para competir en relevo.
Los equipos participan en una cata de sabores a ciegas. Después, Ramsay reta a los equipos a entablar una competencia de relevos.
El Chef Ramsay hace que los concursantes creen un solo bocadillo para crear una audaz primera impresión; los equipos muestran una falta de cooperación durante la cena.
Un nuevo reto para los chefs, tienen que preparar un desayuno gourmet en un food truck de última generación para ochenta personas. El ganador tiene un cambio de estilo y vestuario.
Los chefs tendrán que preparar un platillo fusión de dos cocinas de diferentes países, un gran reto y sorpresas se llevan con el resultado. Se acerca la final y solo dos chefs llegan hasta el último.

Los dos concursantes finalistas deben crear una comida de 5 platos para ser juzgados por personajes distinguidos en la comunidad de comida de Los Ángeles; invitados especiales asisten al servicio de cena; el ganador es elegido.
Los concursantes se enfrentan al desafío, preparar un plato de su autoría; un concursante es llevado al hospital; un aspirante es enviado a casa.
Los 16 concursantes compiten, deberán preparar cuatro piezas de carne con las instrucciones del Chef Ramsay.
El chef Gordon Ramsay utiliza su magia en un restaurante de Tuckahoe, Nueva York, que ha sido renovado, pero aun así tiene un servicio y una comida muy malos.
Ramsay visita el Restaurante y Salón Handlebar en Mount Sinai, Nueva York para ayudar a arreglar el restaurante de Bill y Carolyn LeRoy, que parece que se quedó en la década de 1980.

El chef Gordon Ramsay visita Trobiano's, un restaurante italiano que debe medio millón de dólares. Durante una confrontación con el dueño acerca de la limpieza de la cocina y la calidad de la comida, el chef Ramsay se retira.

El chef Ramsay intenta ayudar a un restaurante mexicano, la Fiesta Sunrise, de gestión familiar para volver a los negocios, pero se encuentra con obstáculos como condiciones insalubres, alimentos en mal estado y cucarachas.

El chef Ramsay viaja a Cranbury, Nueva Jersey para ayudar a dos amigos que compraron un Bistró Francés en el que solían trabajar. Un desagradable descubrimiento en el refrigerador de la cocina obliga a Ramsay a cerrar el restaurante.

Black Pearl, una marisquería en apuros con tres propietarios diferentes al frente de la cocina, acude al chef Gordon Ramsay en busca de ayuda. Uno de los propietarios se resiste al cambio y cuestiona cada movimiento de Gordon.

Los concursantes participan en un reto de pruebas a ciegas. El equipo ganador recibe un viaje a Sea World, mientras los perdedores se encargan de los quehaceres de la casa. En la noche, los equipos crean menús originales.
Un ingrediente hace que algunos concursantes se quebranten; los equipos se unen para completar un servicio durante una cena teatro.

In 1944, Jewish industrialist Joseph Krauzenberg (Martin Landau) and his wife, Rachel (Judy Parfitt), prepare to flee Germany, offering money in return for a safe exit from the country. When Heinrich Himmler (Danny Webb) and Adolf Eichmann (Steven Mackintosh) arrive to conduct the final financial agreements, their suspicions that the Krauzenbergs' servants, Hans (Kenny Doughty) and Ingrid (Caroline Carver), are working against the Nazi regime endanger the wealthy couple's escape.
After a friend's (Julianne Moore) child dies while in her care, a woman (Sigourney Weaver) suffers severe depression and is later accused of sexual abusing a neighbor's son.

Charlie (Michael Douglas) gets released from an insane asylum and moves in with Miranda (Evan Rachel Wood), the young daughter he left behind. Charlie believes that there is treasure hidden beneath the local Costco, so he puts together a plan to unearth the loot. By convincing Miranda to quit her job at McDonald's and instead work at the wholesale store, he is able to obtain a key. Although Miranda is skeptical, she helps her father with his irrational quest.
A former thief (Nicolas Cage) has just 12 hours to come up with $10 million after his former partner (Josh Lucas) kidnaps his daughter and locks her in a cab.

Richard Feynman (Matthew Broderick) is a talented young physics student at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology when he meets Arline Greenbaum (Patricia Arquette). They quickly fall in love and plan on getting married. But when Arline discovers she has tuberculosis, and Feynman is hired by the government to work on the creation of the atomic bomb, his faith in science is thrown into doubt. This true story about the Nobel Prize-winning physicist was directed by Broderick.
A corporate raider (Christopher Walken) and his henchman (Willem Dafoe) use a chanteuse (Asia Argento) to lure a scientific genius away from his employer and family.

Gertrude Baniszewski, a divorced mother of several children, agrees to take care of two girls, Sylvia and Jennie, while their parents travel with a carnival. Though her eldest daughter is the real troublemaker, Gertrude vents all her bitterness and frustration on innocent Sylvia. Gertrude imprisons the girl in the basement and tortures her, eventually encouraging her children to follow suit.
Home for her mother's funeral, a New York designer (Sharon Lawrence) begins sleeping with her best friend's (Harley Jane Kozak) 18-year-old son (Brian Austin Green).
An actor travels to Spain to find a playwright.
Frost fears the presence of a serial killer when a helpless old woman is murdered without motive.
Frost links the death of a young drug addict to an intriguing case of blackmail involving a prominent doctor.
Davies falls victim to a cruel practical joke; death of a medical researcher.
Davies suspects a client of a dating agency in the murder of an Albanian refugee.
A former rival is suspected in the death of a mobile phone entrepreneur at a reunion.
A police detective (Joseph Bologna) teams up with a Cajun hunter (Richard Lynch) to find a giant killer-reptile in the city sewers.
Filmmaker John Carpenter introduces a trio of terror tales: "Unleaded," "Hair" and Tobe Hooper's "Baseball Man."
(1959) A mad scientist keeps his fiancée's severed head alive while he searches for a suitable body. With Jason Evers, Virginia Leith, Adele Lamont.

Apollo 17 was the last U.S.-sponsored lunar voyage -- or was it? Hours of found footage, classified for decades, point to a subsequent moon mission -- Apollo 18 -- that ended very badly. Astronauts John Grey (Ryan Robbins), Nathan Walker (Lloyd Owen) and Benjamin Anderson (Warren Christie), on a mission to install radar scanners, discover a Soviet space capsule nearby. The men also discover a dead cosmonaut, and unfortunately for them, learn how he died.
Movie, Science fiction, Thriller, Horror, Mystery
A scientist (Scott Bairstow) finds a monster that devours its prey in the deserts of South Africa.
Spurned by a Marilyn Monroe look-alike (Linda Kerridge), a film buff (Dennis Christopher) becomes a killer costumed as classic screen characters.

Renegade police officer Matthew Cordell (Robert Z'Dar) once roamed the streets of New York City unleashing his murderous brand of vigilante justice upon its denizens before being struck down by good cop Jack Forrest (Bruce Campbell). Now, Forrest is eager to move on from those heinous events, but he is stopped short when a familiar killing spree begins. Though thought dead and gone, Cordell is back from the grave and ready to wreak his merciless havoc once more.
Deadly wasps threaten a small town after a scientist (Michael Shanks) accidentally releases them.
On a trip to Colombia, a group of college students encounter a sixty-foot boa constrictor, hungry for blood.

Assailed by nightmarish visions, Alex Whitaker (Paul Le Mat) and his fellow psychics descend on the Bodega Bay Inn. There, they discover that their compatriot Neil (Jimmie F. Scaggs) has apparently committed suicide. But, as the gruesome visions continue, they sense that there's still something sinister afoot. When they find themselves hunted by a band of homicidal marionettes created by twisted puppeteer Andre Toulon (William Hickey), they discover they're right.
A wild animal goes on a bloodthirsty rampage on the Appalachian Trail.
Two estranged brothers become obsessed with gaining access to an unexplored cave, despite the horrors they encounter during their excavation.
Los equipos deben capturar a unos pollos y preparar cuatro platillos diferentes con los ingredientes que se ganaron en la ronda previa.

El reto consiste en cocinar con lo básico, al vapor, hervido o escalfado, cada participante debe preparar una proteína y hacer un platillo espectacular. En el servicio de este capítulo servirán sashimi en la mesa.
Los restantes 12 concursantes compiten en un desafío intenso y enfrentan la eliminación.

Jonathan y Mark buscan trabajo como entrenadores de boxeo para poder ayudar a jóvenes llenos de ira. Mientras tanto, reaparece Morton Clay, también conocido como "el jinete enmascarado", acompañado de sus amigos.

Jonathan se encuentra con Sara, una joven cantante que desea saber más sobre su madre muerta, pero a su padre no le gusta hablar de ella. Sin embargo, la vida de Sara puede cambiar cuando un secreto sale a la luz.
Un atleta llamado Dick queda postrado en una silla de ruedas luego de un terrible accidente. El joven necesita la ayuda de Mark y Jonathan, pero también de Eleanor.

Mark y Jonathan ayudan a Barry, un heredero que debe hacerse cargo del hotel de su padre. Al mismo tiempo, debe decidir entre dos mujeres que lo desean: una antigua compañera de clase, y una mujer que trabaja en el hotel.
Jonathan y Mark van a una cafetería para desayunar y son molestados por ser forasteros. Ambos investigan la desaparición de un viejo amigo de Mark. Jonathan encuentra el auto de Charly enterrado.

Jonathan conoce a Liby, de la que se termina enamorando. Al mismo tiempo, Earl, otro chico interesado en Liby, lleva tiempo tratando de conquistarla, por lo que Jonathan debe tomar una decisión difícil.
Mark tiene un accidente automovilístico y queda herido. Jonathan, entonces, lo hace viajar en el tiempo para que pueda salvar a su abuelo y recuperar las tierras de su familia.
Una estrella de baloncesto de la universidad lucha diariamente con su analfabetismo para poder lograr ser becado. Sin embargo, una enfermedad del corazón le impide llevar a cabo sus sueños.
Una mujer moribunda intenta reconciliarse con su severo padre para que su hija ilegítima pueda vivir en un lugar seguro.
La guía de Jonathan ayuda en una conexión amorosa entre Diana, la prima de Mark, y Scotty, un divertido e interesante abogado con tetraplejía.
Jonathan decide hacerse pasar por un hombre millonario, despiadado y soberbio, y por un mendigo amable al que le queda poco tiempo de vida.
Jonathan y Mark le dan una lección a Laurie, una joven actriz cuya fama la está convirtiendo en una mala persona, afectando a su familia y robándole su infancia.
Martin debe tratar a un anciano con un olor horrible. Un presentador de radio local parece tener un problema con la bebida. Julie Mitchell llega a Portwenn.
Culpan a Martín cuando un paciente muere durante un examen. Joan insta a Martín a explicar al viudo las circunstancias que rodean la muerte de Helen.
Martín se ve sorprendido y desconcertado cuando sus padres llegan repentinamente de visita. El examen de Martín a una mujer conduce a un diagnóstico sorpresa.
Llegan Hallie y Christina y marcan el reto: cocinar con cerveza. Cada participante debe crear un platillo con uno o más tipos de cerveza.

Gordon Ramsay les pide nominar a alguien para ser su líder, y para el equipo azul es un proceso rápido, pero para el rojo es un gran problema. El chef Ramsay sorprende a los competidores al pedirles reinterpretar 5 clásicos de comida estadounidense.

Los concursantes tienen el reto de preparar postres para una cena romántica. El equipo ganador se lleva un viaje de lujo a Las Vegas, mientras que los perdedores deben realizar los preparativos para la cena de la próxima "noche de cita".

Los concursantes tratan de demostrar sus conocimientos en una prueba de sabor a ciegas, el equipo ganador disfruta un día de paseo a caballo en las colinas de Hollywood, los perdedores se quedan en la cocina, pelando uvas a mano para la cena.
Tennison es apartada de un caso y se rumorea que podría ser reemplazada. Mientras tanto, la esposa de Marlow es interrogada.

La detective Tennison es transferida a Mánchester, pero no se acostumbra a su nueva situación. Tennison deberá investigar el asesinato de un traficante de drogas que fue abatido a disparos. Un adolescente se confiesa culpable, pero ella duda.
Barnaby y Winter investigan la muerte de un jugador de críquet durante un torneo, pero dudan del motivo del asesinato.
A first date becomes part of a deadly criminal trap.
Pawel Relowicz rapes and kills 21-year-old Hull student Libby Squire in a case that made headlines around the UK.
In March 2005, the Gardaí recovered human body parts from the Royal Canal in Dublin.
Over four months during the late-70s, a killing duo terrorized LA by killing and dumping the bodies of ten women and girls as young as 12 on the city hillsides.
A serial killer brutally snatches away the lives of eight innocent women during a decade-long killing spree in Louisiana.
When the remains of a retired police chief are discovered, police are led to his partner, Marcy Oglesby.
Dena Thompson targets, defrauds and attacks the men in her life before deciding to murder her husband.
Romance novelist Nancy Crampton-Brophy executes the plotline of her own essay "How to Murder Your Husband."
A profile of Richard Roszkowski, the Connecticut triple-murderer who killed his ex-girlfriend, her nine-year-old daughter and another man in a brutal attack in 2006.

In 1999 and 2000, John Eric Armstrong cruised the streets of Detroit, Mich., looking for sex workers; seen as an ordinary husband, father and co-worker, no one in Armstrong's life suspected that he was a serial killer.
Nick sets out to investigate the facility that was once the Western Block Company, a property where people have witnessed shadow figures.
Nick ventures into the Brushy Mountain Penitentiary in Tennessee and the Madison Seminary in Ohio to communicate with the ghosts that are tied to these locations.

Longtime LAPD partners and friends, Brian Taylor (Jake Gyllenhaal) and Mike Zavala (Michael Peña) patrol one of the most dangerous neighborhoods in Los Angeles. Though they may bend the rules, their honor and dedication to the job are unquestioned. Taylor and Zavala always have each other's back, even if Taylor's surreptitious filming of their daily activities for a college course is a bit ill-advised. All hell breaks loose for the officers when they run afoul of a vicious Mexican cartel.

After a string of bizarre bank robberies in Southern California, with the crooks donning masks of various former presidents, a federal agent, Johnny Utah (Keanu Reeves), infiltrates the suspected gang. But this is no ordinary group of robbers. They're surfers -- led by the charismatic Bodhi (Patrick Swayze) -- who are addicted to the rush of thievery. But when Utah falls in love with a female surfer, Tyler (Lori Petty), who is close to the gang, it complicates his sense of duty.

On the day of his retirement, detective Jerry Black (Jack Nicholson) accepts a gift -- an airline ticket to Mexico. But when the body of a murdered eight-year-old girl is discovered in the mountains, Jerry offers his expertise at the crime scene. When an ambitious younger cop wrenches a dubious confession from a simple-minded suspect, the case is closed... but not for Jerry.

Widowed when his FBI agent wife is killed by an extremist group, college professor Michael Faraday (Jeff Bridges) becomes obsessed with the culture of these groups -- especially when his new all-American neighbors, Oliver (Tim Robbins) and Cheryl Lang (Joan Cusack), start acting suspiciously. With each twist, the mystery deepens and questions loom whether Faraday is consumed by fear and driven by paranoia, or whether a lethal conspiracy has been born on Arlington Road.

Detective Sgt. Rick Hunter fights crime in the San Diego area. The wily homicide investigator isn't afraid to break the rules as he pursues justice, though the perpetrators he and his partners are after frequently end up dead. Criticized for its graphic violence, the show also features witty banter between Hunter and his partner.

Jim Rockford is an ex-con and private detective. He was falsely convicted of a crime he didn't commit, but that doesn't stop him from using his ex-con buddies to help him solve crimes. Nothing comes easy for Rockford, but he works hard and usually gets shot at or beat up at least once per episode.

Over a decade later, Maniac Mountain provides another first for the brothers.
The top of the food chain comes into question as the Keefer brothers find themselves between a grizzly and a wolf.
Bloemhof Dam lies deep in the cultural Heartland of South Africa's North West Province, with a multitude of fresh water fish on offer; this is a species hunt that you will not want to miss.

Private air charter is sometimes the only way of reaching true wilderness in Africa. We journey in search of Africa's most ferocious fresh water species, the African Tigerfish, in flimsy boats, surrounded by hippo and croc infested water.

The Gamtoos River near Port Elizabeth on the eastern coast of South Africa, an area known to many as the Windy City, provides a spectacular setting and one of the most important breeding grounds for the multitude of species to be targeted.

The highest Kingdom in the world is also home to the wildest Trout to be found in Africa. Gareth and Jerry trek across the mountains exploring the Senqu and Maletsunyane Rivers before Rhu joins them on the tailwater of Mohale dam, chasing the highland fish of Lesotho.
The high-altitude water of Sterkfontein in South Africa is sight fishing at its finest. The team head to the Free state in search of yellow fish that are attuned to the surface.

This stretch of coastline has claimed more ships and spun more stories of sunken treasure than any in Africa, justifying its title. The team venture along this barren landscape unearthing species unique to this rich coastline despite the inclement...

Every angler has a wish list of species they want to catch or destinations in which they would like to fish. Gareth, Tommo, and Wes each have a different take on what that is before they kick the bucket, join them on their personal quest to fulfil...

Once a year, a phenomenon that is unique to the isle of Goelettes can be witnessed. A fish that can see in panorama is a formidable threat to feeding birds and watching them attack a flying meal is unbelievable.

No richer rivers than those flowing out of the Maluti Mountains can be found in Africa. And their diamond beds are surpassed only by the wealth of golden fins that stream past the riverbanks, being the reason we go prospecting there.

The mesmerizing coral flats of St Francois Island are the hallmark of this marine sanctuary and the diversity of the life it supports is a true testament to the conservation ethos of its stewards. It's a Blue Safari with unparalleled fishing.

The WildFly crew hike the mighty mountains of Lesotho in search of virgin waters that hold trophy Brown Trout. The harsh terrain and unforgiving weather conditions didn't make it easy, but the crew battled it out.
Elk calls echo through the mountains of Colorado; as night falls, Laramy gets within shooting range of a huge elk.

Laramy tracks a big cat in the mountains of Montana.
Springtime begins as Laramy honors the history of the mountain men by trapping for beaver and other critters.
Deep in the Alaskan territory, Laramy hunts for caribou until a severe accident with the Hawken throws the whole hunt into question.
Laramy can't let his injury slow him down; he recaps the incident before rolling up his sleeves to carry on hunting the mountain man way.
Laramy takes a trip to a master blacksmith for new horseshoes.
With a tag in pocket, Laramy takes to the mountains of Idaho on the hunt for the elusive elk.
Winter trapping requires different skills than trapping in the spring.
Laramy hunts the steep climbs of Idaho for mountain whitetail; hunting in the mountains the old way makes for a tremendous challenge.
A real outdoorsman uses every part of the kill, and Laramy shows why skinning and tanning is such an important part of the mountain man life.
Laramy shows us how the mountain men hunted in the 1800s, where unusual skills and stalking techniques were needed not only to succeed in the hunt, but to survive the harsh winters.

Host Kali Parmley and the "Wild Upland" cameras head to Tom Loy of Tallgrass Gordon Setters, in South Central Idaho; Tom has bred a great line of Gordon Setters that range hundreds of yards ahead in the wide open and rough terrain of rural Idaho.

It's Easter and the biggest gardening weekend of the year. The team give plenty of advice and inspiration - from large projects to tackling weeds. At Longmeadow, Monty is getting started on the vegetable plot, where he recommends a palette of potatoes for delicious summer crops. He also returns to his newly created pond, where he is showing how to conceal the liner with an attractive edge.

Monty is preparing for spring colour as well as harvesting pumpkins and squashes. Carol Klein visits comedian Joe Lycett at home, and together, they plant up a container packed with layers of colourful bulbs. Toby Buckland visits Sue Kent's garden near Swansea to help out with autumnal maintenance.

Monty Don tackles the perennial problem of what to grow in the shade beneath a tree, Carol Klein has a look at the crocosmia, and we meet a gardener in Derbyshire who has spent a lifetime growing and showing gladioli.

With the arrival of October, it is time to start thinking about getting some onions and garlic in the ground, and Monty Don shares his secrets on how to get a successful crop. Elsewhere, Carol Klein takes first-time gardeners Dan and Dominique for a day out in Devon. They are on the hunt for some seasonal inspiration for their new garden and what better place to look than RHS Rosemoor.

Monty propagates succulent plants, revisits his container vegetable garden, and gives advice on how to get a good crop of pumpkins. Adam looks a new garden at RHS Hyde Hall in Essex, and Rachel visits a garden of vibrant colours in Wiltshire.

At Longmeadow Monty is planting bulbs in pots and around the garden for an explosion of spring colour. Carol Klein travels to Yorkshire where she has a close look at the enormous colour range and form of a late season perennial, the salvia. Mark Lane is in Oxfordshire looking at how ornamental grasses can be used in planting design to create exciting combinations.

Monty plants for pollinators in the Wildlife Garden and trims his box topiary cones. He also takes succulent leaf cuttings and continues the summer veg harvest. Meanwhile, Carol Klein visits stunning Italian-influenced gardens in Gloucestershire.
Monty's dividing his Pulmonaria and gives advice on frost-protection, Joe visits a tropical oasis outside Bristol, and Carol looks at Rowans from around the world.

At Longmeadow this week, Monty reaps a harvest from the vegetable garden, plants up a seasonal pot and gives a masterclass on how to make the perfect compost. Adam Frost travels to York to meet a couple who took on 20 acres of land and filled it with flowers.

After an extraordinary season, Monty's orchard has a bountiful harvest of apples and he gives advice on how to pick and store them. Frances Tophill makes a final visit to her shared allotment and joins in with the festivities at their annual show. Adam Frost visits the RHS garden Wisley where he meets the Curator to discuss the effects of summer. Nick Bailey investigates knotweed, one of the most pernicious weeds in the UK, Arit Anderson provides inspiration for colourful late season containers.

As Monty brings in the summer harvest, he gives advice on what to sow to keep the crops coming up to the end of Autumn. Carol Klein visits a woman who is losing her eyesight and gives her recommendations of plants that will be a feast for her senses.

Monty's in the jewel garden showing which plants need protection from the elements now and which ones can be left until after the first frosts. He also plants out berried shrubs to help feed wildlife in the winter, harvests pumpkins and shows how to make use of fallen autumnal leaves.

A celebration of people who are growing their own, from vegetables to flowers, across the UK. At Longmeadow, Monty shares tips and advice on how to get the most out of bargain plants. Meanwhile, Joe visits an extraordinary food project in Bristol.

With autumn fast approaching, Monty is preparing the borders for the change of seasons and looking ahead to spring. Adam Frost and Advolly Richmond visit a glorious historic garden in North Yorkshire - Scampston Hall.

This time there's plenty to do to prepare for the season to come, and Monty Don is clearing out spent crops and mulching his asparagus. Joe Swift's been to visit keen gardeners, Wayne and Geraldine Hemingway, to see how they combine sustainability with their designer-style. Carol Klein's exploring the history of the rose at Coughton Court, one of our best rose gardens and Monty plants a new rose of his own. What happens when you have to downsize and leave your much-loved garden?

Adam Frost is at home sharing his love of ornamental grasses, tackling the problem of building a patio on a slope and giving some inspiration on what to plant at the base of a wall. In Margate, the team visit a man who has come up with a unique way of using a shed roof to grow vegetables, and they travel to Swansea to meet inspirational gardener Sue Kent, who shows how she has designed her garden to enable her to garden successfully despite her upper limb difference.

In the cottage garden, Monty is moving a rose which has outgrown its space and in the vegetable garden he gives advice on what to plant now for spring. He also finds out more about the mysterious world of earthworms and discovers why they are vital for the garden.

Monty shows how to stake dahlias, sows seeds of perennials and celebrates an abundant vegetable harvest. The team meet a landscape designer in Cornwall who creates gardens that are not only sustainable but also beautiful and edible.

With autumn just around the corner, Adam takes stock of his garden and plans ahead for some late-season interest under the supervision of Ash the cat. Plus, Frances visits a garden in Kent where the plants provide a non-stop buffet for insects.

Monty's thoughts turn to spring when he gives recommendations for bulbs to plant that will thrive in pots. He also shows how to prune summer fruiting raspberries. In Norfolk, Frances Tophill visits a gardener who at 97 still gardens every day.

Monty Don has advice on how to successfully store an apple crop so it will last through winter and explains why he thinks it high time wall flowers came back into fashion. With tomatoes now over, Monty clears his greenhouse and plans for next year by planting garlic in the vegetable garden. Meanwhile, Carol is home at Glebe Cottage, dividing her perennials to continue the cost-effective stocking of her new beds.

Monty refreshes a container of overgrown herbs, plants alpines and revisits the shrub and perennial cuttings he took a few weeks ago. Arit Anderson meets a designer who is placing sustainability and the environment at the heart of her gardens.
Monty is back at Longmeadow, getting stuck into more seasonal tasks. Joe Swift heads to Houghton Lodge Gardens in Hampshire renowned for its walled kitchen garden and heritage fruit collection.

The successes and failures of all our gardens begin with the humble seed. This show is packed with know-how about how to sow a seed and ideas about how you could improve your garden this summer. Monty starts by sowing tender vegetables like cucumbers and courgettes which, from unpromising beginnings, will provide a fruitful summer. Plus, Carol gives a masterclass on successful seed sowing.

If you have a shady spot in your garden which is bereft of flowers, then Monty Don has some great suggestions of stalwarts which not only thrive in those tricky conditions, but return year after year. He is also working in the vegetable plot giving his tips on what to sow and plant out now. Meanwhile, Carol Klein discovers the pulmonaria, growing prolifically in the woodlands and verges of the New Forest.

The banquet is finally here. It's the culmination of months of hard work as the winning chefs strive to plate up perfect dishes for the Women's Institute ladies at London's historic Draper's Hall.

Three top chefs from Scotland are out to impress this week's veteran judge and be crowned Scottish champion. Adam Handling has already won a number of industry awards and is full of confidence. His starter sets out to take the diner on a tour of the UK's best producers. He's up against Michael Bremner, who is hoping to impress with contemporary ingredients including Birch sap and Douglas fir oil. Ally McGrath is celebrating his nation's finest produce and making his very own version of haggis.
Three newcomers to the competition create their fish dishes in a bid to be crowned Scottish champion. The standard is so high the veteran judge is moved to tears.

Ally McGrath has been keeping the veteran judge entertained with his very individual approach. Also, the highly competitive Adam Handling has been showcasing the finest produce grown and caught in and around the UK in his menu. Once again Michael Bremner is out to show how inventive he can be.

One chef will go home, and today the veteran judge finds himself with a difficult decision to make. Inventive chef Michael Bremner is recreating the Scottish desserts of his childhood, Adam Handling is sticking with his trademark Asian flavours and Ally McGrath is tempering chocolate for the very first time.

Scotland's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for the judges for the very first time. Both chefs have decided to make changes to some of their dishes, taking on board criticisms made during the week by the veteran judge.

Chef Josh Eggleton is back for a third time. Last year he made the national finals when his starter was shortlisted for the banquet, this year he intends to go one step further and cook at the banquet. One of his rivals last time, Jude Kereama is also back and out to do better than he did previously. The third competitor is newcomer Chris Wheeler who is originally from Swanage in Dorset.

There are some exciting dishes on the menu as the three chefs from the South West tackle the fish course. Chef Josh Eggleton is hoping to impress with an original take on Bolognese, just one of six elements on his complex fish dish.

It is the main course and chef Chris Wheeler is out to show just how theatrical he can be, and his ideas are surprising everyone in the kitchen. No one knows quite what to expect, and the veteran chef is hoping it tastes as good as it looks.

It is the dessert course, and it is Josh Eggleton who has come up with the most ambitious dessert. He is creating his own self-serve ice cream made from vegetables, and making everything from scratch including toppings and syrups.

It is the head to head and the South West region's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. They are joined by guest judge, journalist and restaurant critic, Grace Dent.

Two newcomers to the competition are challenging reigning North West champion Matt Worswick. Adam Reid is head chef at Manchester's Midland hotel and Kim Woodward, who made history when she was appointed Head Chef at the Savoy Grill.

It is the fish course and reigning North West champion Matt Worswick has reason to be confident. However, Kim's confident she has got one up on Matt by baking her own black bread unlike Matt who's taking a shortcut.

It is the main course of the North West regional heat and the scores mean this is a crucial round. Matt Worswick may be the reigning champion, but he is not yet assured of a place cooking for the judges, and he is feeling the strain.

It's the dessert course and the three North West competitors are getting creative, producing some of the most original and stunning desserts. All three chefs are working in a hot kitchen, the tension is palpable, and this time one chef will go home.

The two chefs are cooking for judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton, and guest judge Lady Claire MacDonald OBE. There are standout dishes from both chefs making it a difficult contest to judge.

Three of the finest chefs from Wales are competing to be crowned champion. Two chefs are back for a second time: Phil Carmichael, from Cowbridge, South Wales, is executive chef at Berners Tavern in London, and Adam Bannister is chef and co-owner of Slice in his home city of Swansea. Adam was crowned Welsh champion last year so this year Phil is back with something to prove. He plans to go home raising the flag for Wales. The third chef is newcomer Andrew Birch, also from Swansea.

It is the fish course and newcomer Andrew Birch is confident - he is passionate about seafood. He is celebrating the cockle, which is harvested near his home city of Swansea. Adam Bannister has created an alter ego, Captain Bannister, for his modern take on the old boil-in-the-bag fish dinner, and Phil has chosen to revamp the classic prawn cocktail.

Phil Carmichael is serving up his version of an OBE, a refined take on onions, bacon and egg. Adam is planning to serve up wild boar on a spit, while Andrew turns up the heat when he combines strong Japanese flavours with a traditional roast.

It is the dessert course and one chef will go home. Phil Carmichael is determined it won't be him but not everything is going to plan when he tackles his "Cup of Tea for Ma'am". One of the accompaniments to his Earl Grey panna cotta just won't work. He has to make a difficult decision.

It is the head to head. The two highest scoring chefs from Wales are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, blogger and food writer Rosie Birkett.

Three newcomers are competing to become regional champion. Daniel Smith, a former head chef for the Roux brothers, now runs his own restaurant in his beloved home county of Norfolk. Andrew Scott's worked with the best in the business, and he's concentrating on telling powerful stories as well as delivering perfect flavours. Danny Gill is a former head chef at Daniel Clifford's two-star restaurant Midsummer House.

It is the fish course and the chefs are using some of the UK's best seafood: lobster, salmon and Cornish crab. Danny Gill is a chef who likes to use the very latest equipment to create the most intense flavours. He's going to great lengths to maximise the taste of his cucumber consommé, and it is causing a lot of interest in the kitchen.

Two chefs are cooking venison. Danny Gill is making a venison wellington, inspired by his Dad, a former RAF chef who has served up wellington for royalty at many air force banquets, while Andrew Scott has sourced his venison from the Queen's Scottish estate, Balmoral.

This week three chefs from the central region are fighting to be crowned champion. One competitor will go home, only the two highest scoring chefs will make it through to the judging chamber. Danny Gill is facing his toughest day yet, choosing to make a staggering eight elements for his imaginative dessert.

The Central region's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort, for the very first time. Joining them in the chamber is guest judge Enam Ali MBE, a food entrepreneur who set up The British Curry Awards.

Three of the most exciting talents from London and the South East region are competing for a place in the national finals. Head chef Mark Froydenlund runs Marcus Wareing's two-star restaurant. Russell Bateman is head chef at The Grove in Hertfordshire and Ronnie Murray who heads up the Hix Restaurant group.

It is the fish course and chef Russell Bateman is celebrating the diversity of his beloved home town of London - by combining lobster with jerk spices for an ambitious fish course with seven key elements. Ronnie Murray's taking a risk with an ingredient which is close to the veteran judge's heart and is planning to serve it at three different temperatures, warm, deep-fried and frozen. And two Michelin-starred Mark Froydenlund is planning a novel way to present his dish.

It's the all-important main course and returning contender Mark Froydenlund is banking on it being his strongest dish. Russell Bateman is creating a beef dish, and Ronnie Murray's mixing a crown of lamb with a curried filling.

It's the dessert course and the final chance for three of London and South East's most competitive and talented chefs to get through to the judging chamber, today the veteran judge will send one chef home.

It is the head to head and the two highest scoring chefs from the London and South East region are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. Joining this week as guest judge is Kevin Gould, an award-winning food writer.

Mini Patel is back for a second attempt at the north-east regional title, but he is competing against two young newcomers, Tommy Banks and Chris Archer. In 2015 Mini went home after the dessert course, so he is hoping to keep better control of his nerves this year.

It is the fish course and two chefs, Tommy and Mini, have very similar ingredients - both are cooking mackerel. However, Mini is trying an original beetroot sorbet while Tommy is using wild woodruff and oyster leaf from his own garden. Chris Archer has chosen the king of the sea, turbot, but there is controversy in the kitchen.

It is the main course of the north-east region and overnight there has been a dramatic development. It is a tough and emotional day for the chefs as they react to the news, but they battle on in a bid to present a perfect dish with venison and Wagyu-Angus beef - the meat of the day.

It is a highly emotional day for one of the chefs as he prepares a dish which is inspired by and a tribute to his own great Briton, his late grandfather. However, all does not go to plan, and the chef ends up making one key element three times in a bid to achieve perfection.

The two chefs are cooking for judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton for the very first time. Joining them as guest judge is John Williams MBE, the executive head chef at The Ritz, the only hotel to hold a royal warrant for banqueting.

It is Chris McGowan's third time; however, he is facing tough competition from Mark Abbott, head chef at Daniel Clifford's two Michelin-star restaurant, Midsummer House, and also from Eddie Attwell who has just completed a year as head chef at Ardtara Country House in Upperlands.

Mark Abbott is pushing himself again plating up a complex fish course of the very finest produce. He is calling it Shellsational but at the last minute he forgets a key element. Returning chef Chris McGowan is refining cod and chips and Eddie Attwell is getting classical with the king of the sea, turbot. The repartee is relentless as the chefs jostle for top place on the leader board. Once again there is plenty of emotion as the veteran chef delivers the scores.

It is the main course and returning Chef Chris McGowan is feeling confident, but part of his dish involves making his own venison sausages to serve with a venison rack, and getting it all done in time is straining his emotions. Eddie Attwell is also serving the meat but with a traditional Northern Irish dish called Dock pudding. Mark Abbott is pushing himself again; he is using wagyu beef and serving it with tongue and corn cooked in a variety of ways.

The three chefs from Northern Ireland are cooking their desserts and one chef is on course for a historic score, he could beat his boss - a veteran of GBM - and achieve more marks than anyone has done throughout the history of the competition.

It is the head-to-head. The two highest scoring chefs from Northern Ireland are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, restaurant critic and Editor-at-Large of the Independent, Amol Rajan.

It is the national finals of 'Great British Menu'. Before cooking starts the eight champions are called to London's Southbank to get a sight of the prize, the chance to cook at a banquet held at the Palace of Westminster, in celebration of everyday Great Britons honoured by the Queen. It has a huge impact on every one of the chefs, each is determined to do all he can to get a dish to the banquet.

In the run-up to September 1939, political and economic chaos in the aftermath of World War I allowed Hitler in Germany, Mussolini in Italy and ultranationalists in imperial Japan to seize absolute power.

Germany took just four weeks to conquer Poland, using a new form of warfare, Blitzkrieg. Six armoured tank units known as Panzer divisions, supported by the Luftwaffe, quickly broke through Polish defences.

After the retreat from Dunkirk, Churchill rallied Britain in its darkest hour. Hitler was only just across the channel, but he reckoned without our supreme strategist, the might of the navy and the manoeuvrability of the air force.
The attack on Pearl Harbour brought the country nicknamed the 'sleeping giant', aka America, into the war, and saw the emergence of the aircraft carrier as the pre-eminent weapon of the seas.

Italian dictator Benito Mussolini dreamed of recreating the Roman Empire and making the Mediterranean the centre of a new vast colonial empire, including British-controlled Egypt and Sudan to the south.

With their armies fully engaged on the battlegrounds, the Allied and Axis powers focused their efforts to develop new weapons and new strategies to deliver a knockout blow to the enemy and bring about a quick end to the conflict.
After Hitler's gamble in the East fails, the Soviet Union starts to slowly push back and grow.
Following the days of the last World War, with a focus on Allies' strategy tensions.
Exploring the power struggle between Soviet Union, Britain, and USA for peace, following a chronological order to track their fortunes as a new world order is established.

An examination of how items such as Chinese-style furniture, electrical switches and Thai fish sauce are made.
Discover how mortars and pestles are crafted; see how playsets are made.
Learning how race car oil, plaster moldings, lemongrass oil and fly tying vices are made.
Find out how items such as coconut charcoal, dial indicators, wet downdraft tables and bassoon reeds are made.
How classic car gauges, chocolate marble cake, ghillie kettles and rubber gloves are made.
Exploring how everyday items like pasta dies, blueberries, composting toilets and surge arresters are made.
Exploring how everyday items such as angle grinders, berry baskets and omnidirectional speakers are made.
Cartridge blades; chocolate banana loaves; vending machines; dive computers.
How ultra-thin glass, pallet dismantling machines, cupcakes and seamless stainless steel tubes are made.
Learning how handcrafted and factory items such as potash, leather bracelets, wild rice, and hex key L-Wrenches are made.
Learning how metal nail files, birchbark canoes, cruiser boat hardtops and high-voltage circuit breakers are made.
A small-town sheriff (Bo Svenson) accuses his jail's overnight occupant, McCall and Hunter's prisoner, of assault.
Rick and Dee Dee use a woman to lure a man suspected of killing his crime-boss father.
Rick and Dee Dee's only clues to solving a murder are missing homing pigeons and a dead man's niece (Marissa Mendenhall).
Rick is arrested for the murder of a drug dealer he was pursuing for selling to high-school students.
Rick and Dee Dee McCall race against time and try to stop a bounty hunter before he captures a bank robber.
Dee Dee and Rick decide to find a substitute trial witness when they must protect a sleazy mobster who turned state's evidence.
A motorcyclist murders all those who beat him at a fast-draw arcade game.
A parole officer's murder leads to an ex-convict who claims his cohorts are being systematically slain.
A self-styled crime fighter tracks Hunter and McCall to create a list of suspects to execute.
A New York officer comes to extradite a dealer who could lead the team to a cocaine-ring boss.
New York detective Jack Molinas leads Hunter to a mobster holding Dee Dee and Sally captive.
A colorful shirt and a unique machine gun lead Hunter and McCall to a hired killer stalking double-dealing drug pushers.
Hunter and McCall try to outguess an ex-convict who is stalking jurors who found him guilty of murder.
Hunter and McCall track down a man they believe to be a small-time killer but who is actually a highly skilled international assassin.
A TV reporter's persistence complicates the search for a murderous arsonist.
A sniper killing blondes leads Hunter and McCall to a trail of similar murders stretching back 18 years.
Hunter fears for McCall's life when a pornographic filmmaker, suspected of two murders, lures her to his beach house.
After murder interrupts their Chinatown dinner, Rick and Dee Dee suspect a neighborhood war.
Hunter and McCall travel to a resort to find evidence in the murder of a blackmailer; guests Don Stroud, Stuart Whitman.
The detectives suspect a greedy heir is behind the attempted murder of a rich, elderly man and the successful murder of his wife.
An attacker wielding an acid-filled gun stalks stars of a TV show employing Rick and Dee Dee as technical advisers; guest Jan Murray.
Dee Dee falls victim to a foreign attaché who has already raped and killed a woman under the shield of diplomatic immunity; Hunter is determined to find him.
McCall's attacker flees to his native country and the protection of his powerful father.
A thief who killed his accomplices suspects McCall and Hunter stole $6 million from his impounded getaway car.
Hunter and McCall work through the maze of double-crosses surrounding the fatal plunge of a government witness.

In 1990, Marlene is shot by a clown and detectives try to find a motive for her murder; her husband Michael becomes the prime suspect after detectives learn their marriage was on the rocks, but an anonymous tip leads investigators to another suspect.

Michael's affair leads detectives to investigate his alleged mistress Sheila; a lead on the costume from a store puts Sheila firmly in the frame, but without evidence the case goes cold; then in 2017, new DNA evidence leads detectives to an arrest.

After Sheila's arrest, the prosecution prepares for trial and the stakes are high; the prosecution's case centers on new DNA and fiber evidence; Sheila's defense attorney attempts to get the evidence thrown out.
The first victim, Jeannie, is introduced through the testimony of her closest friends and family.
Experts explore whether there was a missed link made between Jeannie's murder and two more deaths.
The cold case investigation into air hostess Jeeta's death provides hope for the past victims.
The current investigation attempts to provide definitive answers for the grieving families.
One woman escapes the clutches of a New Jersey serial killer; the friends and family of another victim set a trap to deliver the killer to police.
Two elderly women in Los Angeles seem to pull off the perfect murder; when they try to pull it off again nearly six years later, things don't go as planned.
In Palm Bay, Fla., a seemingly innocent man is found guilty of murder and sentenced to life in prison; the strongest evidence against him is a debunked form of forensic science.
One of the most famous cases in modern history ends with a verdict that shakes the nation; questions arise over who is responsible, and what part trial consultants and the media play in the outcome.

Facing 20 years in prison for firing a warning shot, a Florida woman is denied use of a controversial legal defense; learning what went wrong, and who "stand your ground" laws are really designed for.
The release of "The Exorcist" is surrounded by controversy, as reports of fainting theater-goers and mysterious on-set accidents raise questions whether the film itself is evil.
A series of unfortunate events plague the cast and crew during the making of "The Omen," raising concerns that the film might be cursed by the devil himself.

A series of untimely deaths connected to the making of the "Poltergeist" films inspire rumors that the production is cursed; suspicions are stoked by rumors that real human skeletons were used during the making of the film.
Years after actor Bruce Lee's mysterious death is attributed to the Lee Family Curse, his son Brandon's life is cut short due to a tragic on-set accident during the making of "The Crow."
A horrific on-set accident during the production of "Twilight Zone: The Movie" leaves those involved in the making of the film cursed by the memory of the incident they witnessed.
Police inspector Carl Mørck and his assistant investigate a cold case involving a missing woman.
A troubled young woman returns to her hometown of Niagara Falls, where the memory of a long-ago kidnapping quickly ensnares her.
An exploration of the dark myths and legends behind one of the most beloved films in the history of cinema, "The Wizard of Oz."
A look into the making of Roman Polanski's "Rosemary's Baby," and the tragic aftermath following the films release.

Examining the troubled making of Andrei Tarkovsky's science-fiction masterwork "Stalker," and the production disasters that beset the filming: damaged film stock, earthquakes, and a sickness that afflicted the cast and crew.
An exploration of Wes Craven's journey into the secret societies of Haitian Voodoo, zombies, and magic.
A look into the making of what is arguably the most controversial film ever produced: Cannibal Holocaust.

A deep dive into nine films that defy categorization and push the boundaries of horror; great films that entertain and provoke audiences; films that put society under a microscope, making people question not just what they fear, but why they fear it.
The expose of the Hare Krishna movement; investigative journalists uncover a range of criminal activity involving guns, drugs, money laundering, abuse and even murder.

Part 2 in the chilling exposé of the Hare Krishna movement, investigative journalists uncover a range of criminal activity involving guns, drugs, money laundering, abuse, and even murder; adapted from the New York Times bestselling book.

The NYPD identifies a dead girl in Central Park as Jennifer Levin; the search for her killer leads to her prep school friend Robert Chambers; Robert confesses he killed Jennifer Levin accidentally during rough sex.
Robert confesses he killed Jennifer Levin accidentally during rough sex; his mother hires a high-profile attorney who says Jennifer was the aggressor.
Robert's preppy persona begins to crumble; when the Church steps in to support Robert, the judge releases him on bail.
The media jumps on the defense's strategy to make Jennifer seem fast and loose; the prosecution works to establish motive.

When the team is called to investigate human remains found in a convention center owner's bathtub, Sara and Grissom use the case to get close to attorney Anson Wix's star forensic expert witness, just days before David Hodges' trial begins.

Prison transport officer Amber is thrown into an explosive situation, when her formidable prisoner, Tibor, is hunted by his crime syndicate, who are determined to stop him from testifying against them.
Amber strikes an uneasy alliance with her prisoner to protect her family; as the situation escalates, Tibor drags her to a drug den, where she sees him kill without hesitation.
When their driver sells them out, Amber withholds Tibor's lifesaving medication to find out her family's location.
Amber reunites with her family while Tibor faces his mother; Olly's actions put them all in danger.
Forced to abandon her wounded husband, Amber asks Tibor to help save Mia; they join the prison transport team, where they learn the terrifying truth of Pegasus' plan.
Amber's plan to get Tibor to court is put in jeopardy as a game of cat and mouse unfolds across London; the fate of her family becomes paramount.

In Modesto, a young couple in love, booked after fighting with an ex-girlfriend, faces the effects of separation anxiety; in Virginia Beach, a man who blew up a car finds himself face-to-face with a deputy from his past.

In Modesto, Calif., a fight at a marijuana dispensary ends with a stabbing; in Bay St. Louis, Miss., a 22-year-old rapper is delighted by his mugshot, but not by the possibility of spending his birthday in jail.
A man attacks his neighbor, then faces jail time; a defendant ordered to turn himself in makes a run for it; a man has an outburst over his bond amount.

Two neighbors that live just two doors apart decide they should get together for a barbecue; that get-together takes a deadly turn that results in a shocking 911 call and a compelling police interrogation.

A Calgary mother disappeared in March 2015; family and friends turned to police as it was out of character for the 24-year-old to just take off; months later, her body was found in a ditch northeast of Calgary by a road construction crew.

After a frantic welfare call, police find 79-year-old Avanell Cowgill murdered in her home; with no clues except for a trail of strange credit card transactions, investigators hope surveillance video will give them what they need to reveal a killer.
Ray becomes jealous when Fraser gets all the media attention during a terrorist's trial, but both lawmen take center stage after they are held as hostages.
Fraser develops amnesia when he is thrown from the back of a speeding van; Ray struggles to help his partner regain his memory.
The team investigates the possible murder of Jake Sullivan (Tony Hawk), a skateboarder and video-game tester.
When an IRS agent is killed trying to repossess a yacht, and another is shot to death soon afterward, the team searches for the perpetrators in a potential series of murders before tax day.

When a foreign diplomat is killed after sneaking into the U.S. under unknown circumstances, Colin and Bill discover that a rare mineral with potential to disrupt international relations may be the reason he was targeted.

A couple from a small Ohio town are charged with 11 felonies, including the death of their infant son, whose injury-riddled body was found in a well; Jessica Groves claims her son's death was an accident.
An Iowa pig farmer stands accused of impaling his wife with a corn rake; the jury has to decide if it was cold-blooded murder or a tragic accident; Todd Mullis takes the stand in his own defense.
Heather Elvis, 20, went missing on Dec. 18, 2013, and has never been found; Tammy Moorer, Heather's boyfriend's wife, is on trial for her kidnapping.

A defendant claims the pants he was wearing and the drug paraphernalia inside them weren't his; a grieving wife describes the DUI accident that killed her husband; an accused murderer is not happy with his lawyer.

After a failed plea for leniency, an angry mother flips the bird to the media after her son is sentenced; a grieving woman begs the judge to keep her brother in prison; a judge must use his mute button to silence a foul-mouthed mom.
A grieving father stares down the man who killed his daughter; a judge mutes an unruly defendant during a virtual hearing; an arsonist pleads guilty to a decades-old crime.

A judge chastises a defendant for his courtroom outburst; a convicted murderer's mother tells the court that she used methamphetamine with him the day he shot his boss; a defendant threatens to sue the judge after an unfavorable decision.

Elsbeth must separate trick from treat in Sleepy Hollow when a rivalry reaches a ghoulish climax on Halloween night after a suburban housewife butts heads with a new neighbor; Capt. Wagner makes a frightening discovery about his daughter.
La revista electrónica que cubre los mayores eventos deportivos al aire libre del mundo, haciendo que el telespectador disfrute desde adentro las actividades sobre nieve, agua o tierra.
Un espacio en el que se destaca a algunos de los mejores clubes del mundo. Desde su fundación hasta los logros históricos se analiza como estas instituciones han marcado al deporte.

La batalla definitiva por la supremacía. Algunos de los nombres más importantes del fútbol se enfrentan cara a cara, con los increíbles argentinos Maradona vs. Messi, además de la batalla de Brasil con Ronaldo vs. Neymar, y mucho más.
Toda la acción de los partidos de la liga de baloncesto profesional mexicana.
Las mejores selecciones, jugadores e historias de los Mundiales de fútbol, el evento deportivo que cada cuatro años paraliza al planeta.
Un panel de expertos celebra algunas de las épocas y dinastías más dominantes en el deporte y decide quién entra en una alineación de fantasía.
Toda la información del mundo de la lucha libre mexicana, las historias de grandes peleas y la actualidad de los luchadores, de la mano de los protagonistas del ring.

Cobertura de la Liga Mexicana de Béisbol (LMB), el circuito profesional más antiguo del país. Disfruta de una de las competencias de mayor nivel y tradición, donde los mejores equipos buscan la gloria en el diamante.
Los combates más emocionantes del boxeo mundial.
The truckers in the historic four-truck convoy face fire and a thin crossing; after Art Burke's engine dies, he must travel back to Winnipeg with Alex Debogorski over a trail that destroys his truck.
The drivers are ready for what is forecast to be a cold and busy winter, but the tragic passing of legendary driver Darrell Ward leaves the drivers wondering who can take his place.

When a woman disappears in Florida, her friends uncover a hidden life filled with new relationships and secrets. As investigators follow the trail, suspicion shifts toward someone in her inner circle who may know more than they admit.

When an Auburn University graduate disappears, her tight-knit group of friends falls under suspicion; as investigators chase leads and rumors spread, distrust grows, until new evidence reveals a truth about someone close to her.
A teenager agrees to fix his friend's computer, then vanishes.

In Richmond, Va., a love triangle tears apart a group of gay girlfriends and leads to murder; investigating this senseless and sadistic killing, detectives uncover a plot fueled by lies, gossip and a thirst for revenge.

In Colorado, police check in on a married couple and discover a grisly double murder; worse, the couple's teenage grandson is nowhere to be found; investigators uncover a much more sinister plot than a robbery gone wrong.
A young mother is murdered inside her home, and her family hopes to help put her killer behind bars.
The police look to find the killer of an unidentified woman found bound, frozen and shot to death in the mountains of Utah.
Police must connect the crime scene evidence from two eerily similar murders to put one vicious killer where he belongs - behind bars.

A 7-year-old cheerleader vanishes at a small town in Kentucky's biggest youth football game of the year; when she's found murdered, panic takes over and every parent fears that the worst kind of predator is among them.

When a popular teenage dancer suddenly disappears one day after practice, police have few leads until one of the dance team members reveals that a man stalked her just days before her best friend's disappearance.

As coach Joe Paterno turns Penn State into a football powerhouse, a serial rapist from the team's ranks preys on multiple co-eds; when the justice system fails to put an end to his attacks, many wonder if Paterno's football machine protected him.

Mindy Morgenstern, a college student and waitress, is found strangled and stabbed in her own apartment; family, friends and the entire town of Valley City, N.D., help law enforcement identify the monster who committed this violent crime.
Bride-to-be Patricia Richmond is found bound and murdered at her future in-laws' home in the resort town of Steamboat Springs, Colo.

After locals smell charred meat, police find burned remains in an abandoned mining pit in the town of Hibbing, Minn.; before they can investigate who committed the crime, they must first identity the body.
Joy Dishneau plans on becoming a small business owner in the Ozarks, but she is found murdered in her own shop, and all of her employees become suspects.

After the murder of a rural Virginia couple and the disappearance of their adult son, detectives wonder who could have acted with such rage; when the son resurfaces, investigators come face to face with a true psychopath.

After the murder of a successful executive one night in Connecticut, her case goes cold; four years later, a troubled man appears, ready to confess; investigators uncover this was no ordinary murder and that he's an impulsive psychopath.

A young man's confession to participating in a plot to murder another teenager stuns police in a small Florida town; detectives uncover a plot involving a manipulative ex-girlfriend and a young psychopath with the desire to kill.

When a loving husband turns up murdered in his Loveland, Ohio home, the prime suspect is his troubled wife, who claims to have little recollection; detectives uncover her story is nothing but the manipulation of a vindictive person.

A road rage incident turns deadly as an elderly man is beaten to death by a teenager who claims he was acting in self-defense; detectives not only find holes in his story but uncover that he is a remorseless and manipulative psychopath.

Terror rocks an Ohio town when a mother, her two kids and a close friend vanish; investigators track down the prime suspect and uncover a house of horrors; detectives find themselves dealing with a psychopath with a bizarre obsession.

Police catch a break on three cold case murders when emerging DNA technology makes a stunning match, a 73-year-old man who's been in prison since 1993; detectives interrogate the frail man whose harmless façade is hiding a murderous psychopath.

A teenage couple goes on the run after an attack on the boy's sister; a search leads officers to the girl's grandparents' home, where they find the bodies of the elderly couple and uncover a fantasy killing concocted by the psychopathic lovers.
