Challenger Kouji Yamada left the prestigious Tokyo University for a life as a chef; he now battles it out with Iron Chef Sakai while his mentor looks on.
Hisao Odachi, the founder of the relatively unknown field of yakuzen cooking, comes to Kitchen Stadium and must make dishes in his showdown with Iron Chef Chen.
In a dessert battle suited for Valentine's Day, one chef reigns supreme when Fuyuko Kondo, the 4th female challenger, takes on Iron Chef Sakai.
Kandagawa brings another female challenger, Yoshie Tobe, into the ring against Iron Chef Chen; it's a soybean battle of the sexes.
Masuo Suzuki, a challenger from Kihachi, a restaurant Iron Chef Michiba used to go to for ideas, comes into Kitchen Stadium to issue a matsuba crab challenge.
Iron Chef Chen takes on challenger Kunihiko Hashimoto, an authority on Japanese cuisine and beloved student of well-known Japanese chefs, for a taro potato fight to the finish.
Iron Chef Sakai faces a challenger known as "Mr. Gourmet"; Komine is a world-class vegetable chef who feels right at home with the secret ingredient.
Zeityen Wan, the former chef to Deng Xiaoping, hopes to make magic with his noodle dishes in just one hour.
The challenger is the first pizza expert to enter Kitchen Stadium; he tries to create a pizza with squid.
Shigeo Yuasa is the head chef of the Okayama International Hotel; with test tubes and litmus papers, Yuasa uses shocking cooking techniques to get his meals to exacting pH levels.
Chiyo Cho has the support of the people of Kobe as he challenges Iron Chef Chen to a titanic tofu tussle.
Called the "Rokusaburo Michiba of the Atami region in Japan," challenger Kunio Santo battles it out with Iron Chef Sakai in the battle of clams.
Former challenger Kandagawa retaliates against the Iron Chefs by sending his head chef, Keisuke Tamano, who challenges Michiba to an ultimate grudge battle.
Chairman Kaga welcomes Korean cuisine for the first time to Kitchen Stadium; Lee Myong Suk is the female evangelist of Korean cuisine in Japan.
The old and new of French cuisine battle each other; challenger Isao Yanagidate opens the door to a long-term battle between Club Mistral and Club des Trentes.
Challenger Etsuo Joh, the god of sauces in classic French cuisine, takes on Iron Chef Japanese Rokusaburo Michiba.
Chairman Kaga invites the very first diner cook to compete at Kitchen Stadium; Katsuo Omiya, trained in the French tradition, challenges Iron Chef Sakai to a tearful battle.
Dissatisfied with the results of their last encounter, Club Mistral is back for a rematch; Kazutaka Okabe challenges Sakai to a rematch of extreme grandeur.
In this battle of blue crab, challenger Akaboshi Sou -- a favorite cook of the royal family -- takes on Iron Chef Michiba.
The esteemed chef and owner of the Italian restaurant Sabatini in Roppongi has sent his protégé, Yukihiro Noda, to go head-to-head with Iron Chef Chen in a fierce battle of sardines.
In the battle of sole at Kitchen Stadium, Iron Chef Sakai faces off against chef Takayoshi Kawai, who heads the kitchen of the Pan Pacific Hotel in San Francisco.
Returning to Kitchen Stadium is the prestigious and young Japanese chef Haruyoshi Omino; Omino's specialty is creating formal Japanese dishes, and he goes up against French-trained Iron Chef Sakai.
Chef Li Jinlun, the world-renowned master of Cantonese food from the prestigious Mandarin Oriental Hotel in Japan, heads to Kitchen Stadium to battle against Iron Chef Chen.
Koichi Tabata, a wandering chef who has worked in over 200 restaurants in Japan, challenges Iron Chef Chen in the battle of eggplant.
Cooking show celebrity Hisama Hirano is invited to Kitchen Stadium to go head-to-head with Iron Chef Chen.
One of the fastest-rising chefs from Kyoto, the ancient capital of Japan, chef Kenji Kaji is invited to battle with Iron Chef Michiba at Kitchen Stadium.
Cuomo brothers face Iron Chefs Sakai and Michiba in fierce Italian-inspired tag-team culinary battle tonight.
Female chef Yoshiko Takemasa is so fastidious that she only cooks fish caught by rods, not nets, to ensure no bruising.
Chef Joel Bruant, an apprentice of the emperor of French cuisine Paul Bocuse, hopes to once again defeat Iron Chef Sakai.
Minoru Noda has traveled all the way from Los Angeles to challenge Iron Chef Michiba in an ultimate Japanese battle.
Chairman Kaga brings in Philippe Aubron, a French chef from Provence, to challenge Iron Chef Sakai in a heated crayfish battle.
An old timer's one-liners don't impress the jailhouse staff; a woman is booked for assaulting her boyfriend; two combative inmates end up in restraints.
A shoplifter fakes a heart attack, a paranoid man blames the FBI, a combative woman apologizes.
A DV suspect caught his wife cheating, a heartbreaking phone call, a female crashes the men's holding area.
A combative suspect refuses a blood draw; an erratic tirade; a woman returns to jail hours after release.
An angry inmate trashes his cell, a woman bites a deputy, a smooth-talking man jokes his way through booking.
A transgender prisoner erupts in a profanity-filled meltdown, an elderly arrestee is worried about her dog.
A prisoner sucker punches a sergeant, an inmate gambles for a solo cell, bizarre excuses abound.
A suspect spits on deputies before getting pepper-sprayed, a combative woman refuses to cooperate.
A threatening suspect begs for his mom, a fugitive refuses to face facts, an angry woman screams at deputies.
A prisoner covered in feces forces a hazardous cell extraction; a combative man faces animal cruelty charges.
A suspect swallows coins, a desperate man fakes a bomb threat, a lucky nickel holds hope, a medical emergency.
An angry man refuses to cooperate during the booking process; a man claims to be part of the "international police."
A woman fights with a nightclub security guard after a waitress refuses to be involved in a threesome with her and her boyfriend.
A scantly clad woman busted for using a fake ID; a meth addicted prisoner breaks down; an intoxicated woman lands in isolation.
A man claims he is a law school student; one man believes he is an alien; a family reunion ends with one husband bruised and bloodied.

Guards uncover a woman's grooming aids hidden in an unlikely place; a tourist-turned-inmate threatens to sue police; a drunk driver who crashed his car into a wall wakes up to find X-rated artwork drawn all over his body.
Welcoming an eccentric regular back to jail; a man fleeing Mexico details the horrors he escaped; a young woman describes her lucrative stint as a stripper.
A man claims of royal lineage during a combative booking process; after resisting officers and harboring a vicious animal, a man is arrested; intoxicated individuals create havoc for officers.

Uncooperative and agitated, a man complains officers are violating his rights when he's not allowed to count his cash; a 443 call is issued and a deputy desperately needs help; a sergeant responds to a bloody fight.
A search uncovers a kinky stash; two unruly inmates invade each other's personal space; a jaywalker has a tough time keeping his pants up.
A testy man is sent to the isolation cell to "cool off"; teary-eyed young man maintains his innocence; an inmate may have ingested contraband to avoid possession charges.
Officers are forced to use pepper spray on a combative inmate; a woman is arrested for solicitation.
A woman lies hobbled in the backseat of a patrol car after kicking the officer in the face; officers struggle to control an outrageous man; they attend to a woman struck by a drunk driver.

Two cousins arrive at jail together but only one leaves; an inmate who won't cool off; one man realizes that cocaine is not his friend; a street artist ends up in jail after meditating naked in a parking lot.
Offices in jail and on the streets prepare for the arrests and aftermath of New Year's Eve festivities in Las Vegas.
Code Blue alarms sound as inmates start fighting inside the men's jail; an irate man with a huge beard refuses to remove bands inside his facial hair; a man with deep stab wounds stumbles into jail.
An inmate becomes aggressive during a routine pat down; a confused senior citizen thinks the detention center is the site of a poetry slam; two girlfriends come to blows while gambling.
A woman is charged with possession of a controlled substance; a woman denies assaulting her husband; two aggressive cousins threaten police and end up in isolation.
A man is charged with indecent exposure; an inebriated inmate is tied to a chair for his protection.
An intoxicated man thinks the doctors are CIA agents; a homeless karate practitioner's actions land him in an isolated cell; a Canadian man with no pants wants to arm wrestle with the guards.
Deputies assist arresting officers by removing an angry man from their patrol car; violent outbursts plague an arrest; one woman struggles with bail; three drunk men become wildly emotional.
A sloppy and combative drunk; a man tries to run from the police after crashing his car; a man blows all of his casino winnings; tricked by a bail bondsman.
A combative, profanity-spewing man is placed in a padded room; a man arrested for battery claims he was locked out of his apartment because he's gay.
After refusing a breathalyzer test, an irate man bangs his head against plexiglass; a man transforms into a "cell warrior" within his holding pen; soon to be released, an inmate considers the future.
A woman is brought into the detention center hogtied; a disruptive teen is sent to a holding cell; casino valets tip the authorities about an intoxicated woman leaving behind the wheel.
A hyper inmate says he drank a month's worth of coffee in a day; a man arrested for DUI while doing donuts in a parking lot claims he is robbed.
A scantily clad female is arrested for assault; a drug dealer claims that his trade is a boom for the economy.
Toting his guitar, an inmate serenades the officers; one man protests his arrest and states that having cocaine is not a crime; a man claims to be an Iraqi war veteran and challenges his detainment.
A woman faces charges of assault on a cab driver; meth addict recounts her past; mother is charged after leaving her kids in the car.
A belligerent man goes to isolation; a woman is shocked when a pipe is found on her; a man shoplifts his own child.
An inmate serenades guards with a guitar solo; a married couple is charged with passing a bogus prescription; a novice pot farmer gets busted after being stopped by police for a traffic violation.
A man is arrested for forgery and littering; a harmonica player attacks skateboarders; a mother steals diapers.
A man is arrested at a popular theme park for public intoxication; a detainee swallows his earring during processing; officers attempt to restrain a combative woman in custody.
A woman goes to jail after telling police she is frightened by a monkey mask; an intoxicated man has feelings for an officer; an officer finds contraband in a pack of cigarettes during a search.

When Jett then kidnaps Milly and disappears into the wild, Doan must track down and outsmart Jett's gang to save the woman he loves.

This ultimately gets Jake shot and wounded, lands Jerry in jail unjustly and leaves the pair plotting to get revenge on the criminals.

When the bandits abduct the young Felice Newsome (Verna Hillie), it becomes apparent they're responsible for the other disappearances as well. Luckily, Drew and Wabi are there, determined to find and free the captives.

Convinced of his irresistible appeal to women, Texas dishwasher Joe Buck (Jon Voight) quits his job and heads for New York City, thinking he'll latch on to some rich dowager. New York, however, is not as hospitable as he imagined, and Joe soon finds himself living in an abandoned building with a Dickensian layabout named Enrico Ratso Rizzo (Dustin Hoffman). The two form a rough alliance, and together they kick-start Joe's hustling career just as Ratso's health begins to deteriorate.

In a violent, near-apocalyptic Detroit, evil corporation Omni Consumer Products wins a contract from the city government to privatize the police force. To test their crime-eradicating cyborgs, the company leads street cop Alex Murphy (Peter Weller) into an armed confrontation with crime lord Boddicker (Kurtwood Smith) so they can use his body to support their untested RoboCop prototype. But when RoboCop learns of the company's nefarious plans, he turns on his masters.

In a not-too-distant dystopian future, when man's most precious resource -- oil -- has been depleted and the world plunged into war, famine and financial chaos, the last vestiges of the law in Australia attempt to restrain a vicious biker gang. Max (Mel Gibson), an officer with the Main Force Patrol, launches a personal vendetta against the gang when his wife (Joanne Samuel) and son are hunted down and murdered, leaving him with nothing but the instincts for survival and retribution.

Lovable Englishman Charles and his group of friends seem to be unlucky in love. When Charles meets a beautiful American named Carrie at a wedding, he thinks his luck may have changed. But, after one magical night, Carrie returns to the States, ending what might have been. As Charles and Carrie's paths continue to cross -- over a handful of nuptials and one funeral -- he comes to believe they are meant to be together, even if their timing always seems to be off.

Fifteen-year-old Charlotte Flax (Winona Ryder) is tired of her wacky mom (Cher) moving their family to a different town any time she feels it is necessary. When they move to a small Massachusetts town and Mrs. Flax begins dating a shopkeeper (Bob Hoskins), Charlotte and her 9-year-old sister, Kate (Christina Ricci), hope that they can finally settle down. But when Charlotte's attraction to an older man gets in the way, the family must learn to accept each other for who they truly are.

New Jersey housewife Roberta Glass (Rosanna Arquette) spices up her boring life by reading personal ads, especially a series of them being placed by a mysterious denizen of New York City named Susan (Madonna). When one of Susan's ads proposes a rendezvous with her suitor (Robert Joy) at Battery Park, Roberta secretly tags along. But when her voyeuristic jape ends in permanent memory loss and a new jacket, Roberta begins to gather a lot of unwanted attention from some unsavory characters.

Gunfighter Wild Bill Hickok (Jeff Bridges) travels the frontier, gaining fame and enemies in roughly equal measure. He sometimes meets up with his friend and occasional lover, Calamity Jane (Ellen Barkin), and he headlines for a while in a traveling circus. Along the way, he meets Susannah (Diane Lane), his one true love, but spurns her for the outlaw life. With his health deteriorating, Bill rides into Deadwood, S.D., as his past catches up to him.

Dillon (Peter Mullan) is a pioneer who defied the harsh winter in search of rumored gold. Having amassed unimaginable riches, he runs a thriving mining town called Kingdom Come. But the blind ambition and greed that drove him to succeed finally catches up to him with the arrival of 3 strangers. Dalglish (Wes Bentley) a surveyor looking to expand the railroad threatens the future of the town -- and 2 women from Dillon's past hold a secret that could be his undoing.

In Cuba, a band of Buffalo Soldiers, led by the intrepid Jesse Lee (Mario Van Peebles) and joined by a gambling white soldier (Stephen Baldwin), is sent on a suicide mission to intercept a shipment of gold from enemy troops during the Spanish-American War. When they discover that the racist white officer who sent them, Col. Graham (Billy Zane), meant to betray them, they are forced to shoot their way to freedom. Upon escaping, they embark on a dangerous quest across the American frontier.

Apache Natives are after Ellen (Bibi Andersson), her baby, and her husband, William (Dennis Weaver). The family crosses paths with Jess (James Garner), a man who is trying to find out who killed his own wife, a Native American woman. He begins to travel with the couple, but the trailing Apaches soon chase them all into a canyon. Jess is able to escape the situation and alert nearby soldiers. In the process, he also discovers a shocking revelation about his wife's death.

While the Earp brothers may have won the gunfight at the O.K. Corral, they didn't escape unscathed for long. Seeking revenge over their fallen comrades, members of the Clanton gang go after the Earp family, gunning down both Virgil and Morgan Earp. But they don't succeed at getting Wyatt. Now it's his turn to seek revenge. With Doc Holliday by his side, Wyatt forms a posse, and they won't rest until every member of the Clanton gang is dead.

In this take on the gunfight at the O.K. Corral, Doc Holliday (Stacy Keach) travels to Tombstone, Ariz., with prostitute Katie Elder (Faye Dunaway). Although the trip is difficult because Doc is ill with tuberculosis, they eventually reach their destination, where Holliday is reunited with his old friend Marshal Wyatt Earp (Harris Yulin), who has been clashing with the Clanton gang. Tension between Earp and the Clantons rises until their infamous final showdown brings it to a head.

During a bank robbery by the legendary James-Younger Gang, Ed Miller (Dennis Quaid) impulsively kills a man, much to the displeasure of leader Jesse James (James Keach), who insists that the gang scatter until the heat is off. The groups of brothers go their separate ways, with Cole Younger (David Carradine) considering settling down with his feisty girlfriend, Belle Starr (Pamela Reed). But they soon regroup for an ill-fated bank job in Northfield, Minn., that results in an epic chase.

Upstanding widower "Big Eli" Wakefield (Burt Lancaster) decides to move from Kentucky further west to Texas. He undertakes the journey with just his young son "Little Eli" (Donald MacDonald), but en route they pick up friends like indentured servant Hannah (Dianne Foster) and schoolmarm Susie (Diana Lynn), a potential love interest. This motley crew's path is difficult, and they face many obstacles, not the least of which is nasty frontiersman Stan Bodine (Walter Matthau).

Johnny Hawks (Kirk Douglas), a Civil War veteran renowned for his prowess in battling Native American tribes, is hired to escort a group of white settlers. But when lowlife Wes Todd (Walter Matthau) discovers that nearby Sioux are hiding a trove of gold, he becomes obsessed with locating it -- which quickly stirs up trouble with local Sioux warriors. However, Hawks, preoccupied with a pretty Sioux woman, Onahti (Elsa Martinelli), doesn't realize that there's conflict until it's too late.

As the winter of 1867 approaches, Denver inhabitants led by chronic drunk Oracle Jones (Donald Pleasence), who has visions when inebriated, realize with horror that their supply of whiskey will run out before the snows melt. Oracle devises a plan to bring cases of whiskey from a distillery, but is thwarted at every turn. A temperance leader (Lee Remick), three Sioux Indians, and the U.S. Cavalry become interested in the shipment, and a sandstorm and quicksand add to the difficulties.

The Zachary family live quietly on a cattle ranch in post-Civil War Texas. A stranger (Joseph Wiseman) appears and disturbs their bucolic existence by spreading a malicious rumor that their adopted daughter, Rachel (Audrey Hepburn), is a Kiowa Native American. Soon, the Zachary brothers (Audie Murphy, Burt Lancaster) and their mother (Lillian Gish) must defend themselves from both racist whites and vengeful Kiowa.

Following the American Civil War, veteran Benjamin Trane (Gary Cooper) and gunslinger Joe Erin (Burt Lancaster) are just two of many men who head to Mexico as mercenaries. When Emperor Maximilian (George Macready) recruits their services, they reluctantly work together, since the price is right. Trane and Erin are to escort Countess Marie Duvarre (Denise Darcel) to Veracruz -- but when they find a wealth of gold hidden in the stagecoach, the original plan no longer applies.

A team of ghost hunters reaches out to the dead in an abandoned gold mine; numerous sightings and strange disappearances suggest a fearsome yeti inhabits the frozen landscape of the Alaskan mountains.

A sonar recording may prove that a prehistoric monster stalks the seas surrounding Kodiak Island; researchers investigate why thousands of airplanes have disappeared without a trace in the Alaska Triangle.

The Alaskan skies are filled with unexplainable lights and objects, but evidence suggests these extraterrestrial visitors are landing; prehistoric monsters may be alive and well in the Alaska Triangle.
Hostile Sasquatches leave the wilderness behind for Alaska's major cities; a paranormal investigator searches for evidence of ghosts at an infamous haunted hotel.
An underwater alien base may be located off the coast of a quiet Alaskan town; a cannibalistic creature preys upon those brave enough to venture into the Alaska Triangle.
Dark forces disrupt a paranormal investigation at an old fairground near Fairbanks, Alaska; hundreds of Alaskans go missing every year.

Experts make a chilling new discovery when they unearth a 30,000-year-old zombie virus from an icy grave; if this ancient disease is successfully resuscitated back to life, it could cause a catastrophic global calamity.

When strange towers of ice are found growing in a barren, water-starved desert, experts speculate why these structures have uncanny similarities to extraterrestrial formations recently discovered on Pluto's alien landscape.

After a 2,500-year-old mummy is discovered in Siberia, locals report strange, cataclysmic events that point to an ancient curse; using cutting-edge archaeology, experts reveal who this person was and if they've unleashed something sinister.

Three graves are discovered on the frozen beach of an uninhabited Arctic island; the mummified corpses inside may answer a centuries-old mystery of an expedition that was literally consumed by the cannibalistic insanity of its mutinous crew.

A frozen lake deep in the Himalayas melts once a year to expose hundreds of human bones and a centuries-old mystery of astonishing carnage; leaving experts to speculate if it was a single catastrophic event or something much more sinister.

A top-secret military base hidden deep in the ice beyond the Arctic Circle is one of the Cold War's most elaborate cover-ups; recently declassified documents reveal its deadly purpose; the threat it might still pose to all humankind.

A salvage team discovers the mysterious remains of an enormous shipwreck near Cambridge Bay in the icy waters of the Canadian Arctic; experts investigate and uncover a cutting-edge vessel with links to one of the greatest polar explorers in history.

Preserved in the ice of Mexico's highest peak, a group of climbers stumble upon the bizarre, mummified remains of a man in a pinstripe business suit; experts uncover possible drug cartel connections and a plane crash shrouded in secrecy.

An unidentified metal object is found on Kiska Island; a centuries-old gold mining mystery is investigated; in Siberia, a network of ice tunnels is explored; fossils unearthed in the Canadian Arctic lead to the discovery of a new species.

Archaeologists discover an unusual man-made rock formation in the remote Altai Mountains of Russia, and conducting a further excavation, they unearth an ancient log cabin and the mummified remains of two bodies buried deep in the frozen permafrost.

Mountain climbers in California find the body of a U.S. Army soldier; strange bundles of canvas and wood are discovered on an Alaskan mountain; volcanic glass is found in an unexpected place; a vital World War II weather station is uncovered.

Happily married Michael (Kurt Russell) and Karen Carr (Madeleine Stowe) call the police after a failed robbery. Officer Pete Davis (Ray Liotta) arrives and helps arrange the installation of a new security system. The grateful Carrs have Pete to dinner and strike up a friendship. Pete invites Michael to ride with him during a night's patrol and gives him the chance to beat up the burglar. Michael refuses and tells the disturbed cop to stay away, but Pete begins stalking the terrified couple.

A staunch advocate of healthy living, Dr. John Harvey Kellogg (Anthony Hopkins) opens a sanitarium that promotes his progressive, if eccentric, ideas about optimal well-being. Among the clients who arrive at the facility are the opportunistic Charles Ossining (John Cusack), who is keen on marketing Kellogg's cereal, and the wealthy Will Lightbody (Matthew Broderick) and his wife, Eleanor (Bridget Fonda). This comedy is inspired by an actual spa run by Dr. Kellogg at the turn of the century.
A space hero (Reb Brown) puts down mutineers (John Phillip Law, James Ryan) on a huge ship taking earthlings to a far planet.

Austin, Texas, is an Eden for the young and unambitious, from the enthusiastically eccentric to the dangerously apathetic. Here, the nobly lazy can eschew responsibility in favor of nursing their esoteric obsessions. The locals include a backseat philosopher (Richard Linklater) who passionately expounds on his dream theories to a seemingly comatose cabbie (Rudy Basquez), a young woman who tries to hawk Madonna's Pap test to anyone who will listen and a kindly old anarchist looking for recruits.
An evil archaeologist tries to exploit five pygmy dinosaurs that hatched in a family's basement.
Miniature dinosaurs help a boy outwit a malevolent governess who wants to pack him off to a military boarding school.
Pygmy dinosaurs help the owner (Fred Willard) of a miniature golf course fight off bank foreclosure and takeover by his greedy brother (Bruce Weitz).

Jimmy Rabbitte, a self-proclaimed promoter, decides to organize an R&B group to fill the musical void in his hometown of Dublin, Ireland. The band comes together but ends up consisting entirely of white musicians who have little experience with the genre. Even though their raw talent and lofty aspirations gain the group notoriety, the pitfalls of fame begin to tear at their newfound friendships as they prepare for their big show. Based on the novel by Roddy Doyle.
A teacher (Colin Firth), obsessed with soccer and a team that hasn't won a league cup in 18 years, begins a shaky relationship.

In the winter of 1944, American soldiers led by Will Knott (Ethan Hawke) are assigned to capture a small squad of German soldiers posted in France's Ardennes forest. Tired of war, the Americans have already lost half their division and discover that their German enemy is equally unwilling to fight. With Jewish soldier Stan Shutzer (Arye Gross) interpreting, the Germans and Americans agree on a plan that will let the former surrender without violence -- but then, tragedy strikes.

Jobe (Matt Frewer) exists as a malevolent consciousness in virtual reality and seeks to discover the technology to hack into all the world's computers. Jobe contacts Peter (Austin O'Brien), who had been a friend during his corporeal existence, to assist him, but the young man realizes Jobe's evil intent. Peter calls on Benjamin (Patrick Bergin), a brilliant computer engineer, to help thwart Jobe's scheme for world domination, and a battle rages throughout cyberspace and in the real world.

When Helen, a London ad executive, is fired from her job and rushes out to catch a train, two scenarios take place. In one, she gets on the train and comes home to find her boyfriend, Gerry, in bed with another woman. In the second, she misses the train and arrives after the woman has left. Following the first scenario, Helen dumps Gerry, finds a new man and gradually improves her life. Under the second scenario, she becomes suspicious of Gerry's fidelity and grows miserable.
Mix of R&B, rock and dance that emphasizes pop and alternative hits from the nineties.
Todo en la vida de Manuela Mendoza parece estar en perfecto orden, pero pronto recibe una sorpresa muy dolorosa: su prometido tiene una doble vida. Manuela debe decidir entre dejarlo o perdonarlo.

Una muchacha que vende periódicos en una esquina de una avenida concurrida de Caracas tiene dos sueños, llegar a ser una gran ingeniera y ser la novia de un chico guapísimo que suele pasar con su coche por donde trabaja.

Sol, una joven que va en busca de una mejor vida a la ciudad, se enamora del hijo de quien estafó y asesinó a sus padres; ella logra recuperar su fortuna y empieza a cumplir una venganza sin tregua donde no hay diferencia entre amor y odio.
Una joven mujer, Yubirí, busca triunfar en su carrera y en el amor. Una pitonisa le indica que conocerá a su amado, esa misma noche ella conoce a Wilker, un joven cantante, y a Juan Diego.

Irene es una mujer atractiva e inteligente, pero con baja autoestima que conoce a Leonardo, un viudo millonario para quien comienza a trabajar como secretaria. Poco a poco, Irene se enamora de él, pero muchos tratarán de destruir su amor secreto.

It has been many years since the Ghostface Killer cut a deadly path through the town of Woodsboro. In order to get over the trauma of those horrific events, Sidney Prescott (Neve Campbell) has written a self-help book. She returns to Woodsboro for her book tour, and reconnects with old friends Gale Weathers (Courteney Cox) and Sheriff Dewey (David Arquette). However, Sidney's arrival also sparks the return of Ghostface, putting Sidney and everyone she loves in danger.

On Halloween night, three young women and their respective boyfriends head to Hell Fest -- a ghoulish traveling carnival that features a labyrinth of rides, games and mazes. They soon face a bloody night of terror when a masked serial killer turns the horror theme park into his own personal playground.
A teenage Leatherface escapes from a mental hospital with three other inmates, kidnapping a young nurse and taking her on a road trip from hell, while being pursued by a lawman out for revenge.

Ten years ago, an inexperienced coal miner named Tom Hanniger caused an accident that killed five men and put a sixth, Harry Warden, into a coma. A year later, on Valentine's Day, Harry woke up and murdered 22 people with a pickaxe before dying. Now Tom has returned home, still haunted by the past. And something else is back in Harmony: a pickaxe-wielding killer in a miner's mask, who may be the ghost of Harry, come to claim Tom and his friends.

The story of two outcast sisters, Ginger (Katharine Isabelle) and Brigitte (Emily Perkins), in the mindless suburban town of Bailey Downs. On the night of Ginger's first period, she is savagely attacked by a wild creature. Ginger's wounds miraculously heal, but something is not quite right. Now Brigitte must save her sister and save herself.
Brigitte is found and taken to rehab; the wolfsbane serum is a narcotic.

In early 19th-century Canada, orphaned sisters Ginger (Katharine Isabelle) and Brigitte (Emily Perkins) find themselves lost in a forest while riding on horseback. They're rescued by The Hunter (Nathaniel Arcand), a mysterious Native American who takes them back to Fort Bailey. Something strange has happened there, however. The few settlers who remain are suspicious of outsiders and keep tight-lipped about the situation, but Ginger soon discovers their secret for herself.
Heir to a line of werewolves, a teenager (Landon Liboiron) battles a pack of beasts and his own lust for blood.

Bullied at school, neglected at home and incredibly lonely, 12-year-old Owen (Kodi Smit-McPhee) spends his days plotting revenge on his tormentors and spends his nights spying on other residents of the apartment complex. His sole friend is Abby (Chloë Grace Moretz), a strange girl who comes out only at nighttime. Both outcasts, the two form a strong bond. When Abby's caretaker disappears amid a series of gruesome murders, Owen begins to suspect that she is hiding a terrible secret.

Ten years after a plague turns most of the world's population into vampires, a critical blood shortage causes panic and gruesome mutations among the reanimated. Edward (Ethan Hawke), a vampire hematologist, tries to develop a blood substitute when he meets Lionel (Willem Dafoe) and Audrey (Claudia Karvan), two fugitive humans who claim to have a possible cure. Edward casts his lot with them in the hope of perfecting the cure before it's too late.

Cowboy John O'Hanlan (James Stewart) is surprised to learn that someone's left him a business in Cheyenne, Wyo. He sets out to claim it -- and is shocked to discover that it's a brothel. Madam Jenny (Shirley Jones), who runs the place, is dismayed when O'Hanlan wants to close it down, but his plans are derailed when he finds out that a local customer has beaten Jenny. He kills the man in a shootout, and then must protect himself and the girls from the dead man's vengeful clan.

When a yearly high-stakes poker game begins between the five richest men in Laredo, Texas, all other activity in the Wild West town comes to a stop as everyone gathers to watch the action. Recovering gambler Meredith (Henry Fonda), passing through town on the way to San Antonio, gets roped into the game by lawyer Otto Habershaw (Kevin McCarthy). When the stress of the game becomes too much to bear, his disapproving wife, Mary (Joanne Woodward), must step in to save the family fortune.
An orphan grows up to fulfill his duty as bodyguard (Tom Berenger) to Mormon leader Brigham Young (Charlton Heston).

In Colonial America, Jim Smith (John Wayne) leads a group, including the intense Janie MacDougall (Claire Trevor), that tries to figure out who is supplying the area Native American tribes with weapons. He suspects corrupt trader Ralph Callendar (Brian Donlevy), but does not have proof yet. Jim's accusations fall on deaf ears with unsympathetic British commander Capt. Swanson (George Sanders). Worse, Callendar, sensing that Jim is on to him, frames the hero for murder.

After a group of outlaws vandalizes a ranch and injures a ranch hand, their leader, Sims (Frank Hagney), blames a horse named Duke. As the townspeople prepare to execute Duke, John Drury (John Wayne) negotiates a pardon for the animal. Sims, who is in reality a famed killer known as the Hawk, attempts to eliminate John and frame him for a ranch fire. As the angry townspeople search for John, he must prove his innocence and stop the Hawk once and for all.

Just before Bess (Lucile Browne) returns home to the ranch owned by her father, Dan Matthews, robbers attack him and his friend, Sheriff John Higgins (John Wayne) -- and Dan is killed in the gunfight. Convinced that one of his shots resulted in Dan's death, John resigns as sheriff. Former sheriff Ed Williams (George Hayes) convinces John to work for Bess to make up for his error, and he becomes her foreman. John doesn't confide his involvement in her father's death, but Bess soon hears rumors.

A determined prospector, Jonathan Harvey (Paul Kelly) finds gold after years of searching. When he returns to town to tell his partner, Jonathan finds that his friend has died, leaving his son, Tommy (Gary Gray), on his own. While Jonathan's loyal collie, Lassie, stays with the boy, he goes to find help to assist him with his lucrative discovery. However, the new recruit (Bruce Cowling) proves to be a shady character, and before long the ruthless schemer has incurred the wrath of Lassie.

The epic biography of western lawman Wyatt Earp, who at an early age, is taught that nothing matters more than family and the law. He becomes a respected sheriff in Dodge City and Tombstone. Joined by his brothers and Doc Holliday, Earp wages war on the dreaded Clanton and McLaury gangs.
A U.S. marshal (John Wayne) neglects his two sons and finds them mixed up with an outlaw (George Kennedy) in a bank robbery.

In this gritty Western classic, aging outlaw Pike Bishop (William Holden) prepares to retire after one final robbery. Joined by his gang, which includes Dutch Engstrom (Ernest Borgnine) and brothers Lyle (Warren Oates) and Tector Gorch (Ben Johnson), Bishop discovers the heist is a setup orchestrated in part by his old partner, Deke Thornton (Robert Ryan). As the remaining gang takes refuge in Mexican territory, Thornton trails them, resulting in fierce gunfights with plenty of casualties.

On a trip to London with his daughter (Yvette Curtis) for some dirt-bike races, Dr. Matt Younger (Sidney Poitier) meets beautiful dignitary Catherine Oswandu (Esther Anderson) and quickly falls for her. But something is amiss -- strange men seem to be following her wherever she goes, and Younger assumes she's at the center of some political intrigue. His heart sinks when he learns that she has sickle cell anemia, and the men are watchdogs in the employ of her anxious father (Earl Cameron).

Axel Nordmann (John Cassavetes) takes a job as a dock laborer and is continually harassed by his tyrannical supervisor, Charles Malik (Jack Warden). Malik knows a secret from Axel's past, forcing the young worker to endure his boss's torment. Eventually, Axel befriends Tommy Tyler (Sidney Poitier), an African-American co-worker with a managerial job. Tommy teaches Axel to respect himself. However, Malik, a racial bigot, is threatened by Tommy's confidence, and the situation turns violent.
While on shore leave, two sailors stumble upon a nest of sexy vampires.
A nightclub owner (Rudy Ray Moore) declares war on drug dealers after his nephew has a bad trip on angel dust.

Men who return home from the Civil War with hopes of rebuilding their lives find death and destruction.
Medieval samurai Lone Wolf (Tomisaburô Wakayama) works as a hired sword, roaming with his son (Kenji Misumi) in a baby cart.

Eric Sloane (Dennis Alexio) is an American kickboxing pro, helped by his brother, Kurt (Jean-Claude Van Damme), in his quest for glory. But when the two go to Thailand to take on legendary Tong Po (Michel Qissi), the opponent viciously beats Eric and leaves him paralyzed. Swearing vengeance, Kurt tracks down master Xian Chow (Dennis Chan) and begins learning the sport himself while also getting caught up in criminal intrigue involving thuggish crime boss Freddy Li (Ka Ting Lee).
Asian villains pick a fight with a Los Angeles kickboxer whose brother beat them in Bangkok.

Nadie le cree al Abuelo Pitufo cuando habla de junglas y sabanas lejanas, repletas de gatos salvajes gigantes, caballos a rayas, comedores de hojas de cuello largo y extrañas tribus. Pero tiene la ocasión de demostrar que no está mintiendo.
El rey de los Wartmongers captura a los Pitufos dentro de burbujas cuando, por accidente, terminan dentro de su territorio.
Las aventuras de unas pequeñas criaturas azules que viven en armonía en un bosque, que tendrán que luchar contra los malvados planes de Gargamel.
El granjero se encuentra con el genio Gourdy en su jardín, quien causa un desastre, pero de todos modos se le permite quedarse en el pueblo.

Pitufo Armonía ya no es bienvenido en el coro de los pitufos, ya que canta de una manera demasiado desafinada. Sin embargo, Papá Pitufo le entrega un amuleto que le convertirá en un virtuoso del canto.
Los pitufos cruzan sin darse cuenta el río del tiempo, lo que crea un gran desastre. Ahora, tienen que detener el tiempo antes de que el río se seque.

Selwyn y Tallulah son poderosos hechiceros. El problema es que están todo el rato peleándose. La energía de sus discusiones está formando una temible tormenta, y Papá Pitufo debe conseguir que hagan las paces antes de que la tormenta arrecie.

Baltasar lleva a Denisa con Gargamel. Sin embargo, Denisa se encuentra con Sasita en el bosque y se hace amiga de ella. Juntas colaboran para sacar a los pitufos del caldero de Gargamel y demostrar que la valentía no es cuestión de tamaño.

Va a haber un festejo en el castillo del rey y Guillermo invita amablemente a sus pequeños amigos azules al banquete. Sin embargo, descubren que el malévolo chambelán está afanando las posesiones del rey.

Para demostrar lo válido que es su Gran libro de supervivencia en la naturaleza, Pitufo Filósofo se lleva a los pitufitos al pantano. Allí, gracias a su experto consejo, el pequeño grupo se extravía y es capturado por el Rey Verrugoso.
Malcolm, el perverso cazador, ha convertido al rey en un ciervo negro para deshacerse de él. Los Pitufos tendrán que salvarlo.
Gargamel propaga un extraño germen por el bosque que hace toser a todos sin parar. Bebé Pitufo es la primera víctima y todo el pueblo está muy preocupado.
Los delirios de grandeza de Soñador se hacen realidad cuando naufraga y los osos lo descubren, lo coronan como su rey y le piden que derrote a sus temibles opresores.
Una vanidosa duendecilla llamada Periwinkle secuestra a Vanidoso cuando su espejo mágico le dice que él es más guapo que ella.
Exhiben a Tontín y Pitufina en una feria luego de capturarlos. Papá Pitufo hará uso de la torpeza característica de Gargamel para que regresen a la aldea.

Pitufo Labrador es el reticente amo de un genio llamado Gourdy, cuyo entusiasmo por ser servicial es quizá algo excesivo. Tras un nuevo incidente provocado por el exceso de celo de Gourdy, Pitufo Labrador le dice algo que no debería haber dicho.
Fortachón es mordido por una pulga que Gargamel infectó con un elixir de odio. Ahora el Pitufo es egoísta, peleonero y está lleno de malicia.

Los pitufos provocan que todos los colores desaparezcan del mundo al jugar con la rueda de los colores del hada Spectra. Si Papá Pitufo no encuentra una solución y restaura los colores, la pobre hada morirá.
Un duende maligno le da a Pitufina zapatos de baile y luego la engaña para lograr que ella prometa casarse con él.

Cada vez que Pitufo Perezoso se queda dormido, tiene la misma pesadilla una y otra vez: se encuentra en poder de Morfeo, un malvado hechicero que quiere capturar a tantas almas dormidas como sea posible.
La primavera hace que todos los pitufos estén compitiendo por el amor de Pitufina y Gargamel decide hechizarla para que lo ayude a capturarlos.
Los Pitufos intentan evitar el contacto con los humanos. Esta vez, Sasita se hace amiga de una pequeña bruja llamada Melina, cuyos hechizos suelen acabar en desastre.
Los Pitufos se encontrarán con Simón, quien perdió el rumbo mientras intentaba hallar a sus padres, y lo ayudarán a regresar a su casa. Gargamel intentará complicar sus planes.
Papá Pitufo ayuda a Soñador a convertir en realidad su sueño de ser un Astropitufo.
Es la primera Navidad de Pitufo Salvaje y está impresionado por la decoración de la Aldea Pitufa. Pero Abuelo Pitufo y Sasita van a enseñarle el auténtico significado de la Navidad.
El cachorro se porta mal cavando en los jardines de los Pitufos, persiguiendo conejos y comiéndose las trufas de Pitufo Goloso y Papá Pitufo decide que debe ser entrenado.
Los pitufitos liberan a los pitufos de las garras de Gargamel justo a tiempo para llevar a Bebé Pitufo a la ceremonia de su primera palabra. Bebé Pitufo pronuncia la palabra "Gargamel".
Gargamel lanza un hechizo a la nueva cama de Papá Pitufo para que cualquiera que duerma en ella sea transportado al lugar con el que esté soñando.
Manitas y Arquitecto crean un apartamento que resulta ser un emprendimiento inútil.
El malvado mago Gargamel vuelve a estar en problemas. Si no puede reunir una enorme cantidad de oro para el atardecer, le arrebatarán todas sus posesiones.
Una esfera desata un incendio en la aldea.

Pitufo Robotín se siente tan solo que, compadeciéndose de él, Pitufo Carpintero le construye una compañera. El problema es que Pitufa Robotina no sabe que únicamente debe fijarse en su compañero mecánico, o que debe evitar a Gargamel.
La magia de la Navidad se ve frustrada cuando Chlorhydris hechiza a Santa Claus para que no pueda repartir felicidad.

Cuando Escrupuloso, el ayudante del malvado Gargamel, encuentra el Gran libro de hechizos en el sótano de su maestro, le pide poder para convertirse en el mago más poderoso del mundo. Esto supondrá problemas para los pobres Pitufos.
Por accidente, los pitufos quedan enterrados bajo una avalancha que fue provocada por Travieso y su egoísmo.
Natural y Travieso roban la fórmula de Gargamel para crear otra pitufa, para acompañar a Pitufina. Es así como crean a Sassette, que resulta ser bastante problemática.

Cuidar de los animales produce consecuencias inesperadas cuando los Pitufos deciden llevar a un bebé dinosaurio de vuelta a casa, ¡a su propia era! Este es el inicio de una serie de aventuras en las que recorrerán el espacio y el tiempo.
Mientras intenta escabullirse de sus tareas, Perezoso encuentra un antiguo pozo abandonado con una interesante peculiaridad: cualquier objeto que uno baje en el cubo regresa como nuevo.
Los Pitufos llevan a Abuelo Pitufo al castillo del rey para que pueda conocer a Guillermo. Pero, entre una cosa y otra, los Pitufos y Guillermo acaban a bordo de una gran nave vikinga.
Papá Pitufo se marcha por un tiempo, dejando el puesto de jefe vacante, pero Pitufo Filósofo se nombra a sí mismo nuevo líder. Nadie hace caso de las advertencias de Pitufo Bromista sobre Azrael.

America had Al Capone; England, the Kray brothers and Australia - proving once and for all its antipodean sense of humor - has Mark "Chopper" Read. "Chopper" is inspired by the books of Mark Brandon "Chopper" Read, arguably Australia's most infamous former criminal. "Chopper" draws on police records, court transcripts, news coverage and interviews with people who knew Chopper Read.

The first to host are exuberant Jon Shorrock and his wife Julia, who run the four-star B&B Derwent House in West Sussex. As the guests take a quiet gander at their rooms, Andy and Julian have concerns over their carpeted bathroom, worrying it could hide alien hair. Once they've settled in, Jon and Julia split the group up by gender for a glimpse of the local area.

Soul mates Peter and Sharron Sorsky share the warmth of their Liverpool home with the week's guests. On arrival at Kirkby Park B&B, via the industrial estate, Annette is immediately on her guard after noting the CCTV camera on the outside of the house. Things don't get much better during the room inspection, as guests find dust, curly hair, unspecified dirt, stains and a hole in the wall.

Andy and Julian Banner-Price host the competition at their swanky Plas Dinas Country House in Snowdonia, where they've allocated their guests their priciest rooms costing between £190 and £250 per night. Peter and Sharron arrive in North Wales still reeling from receiving their own feedback forms, and immediately begin finding fault with seemingly every aspect of their room, particularly the antique furniture.

The final B&B of the week is Annette McAnespie's Hazelwood Farm in Crake, Yorkshire. Annette is a one woman whirlwind, as she cleans and cooks everything herself in her four-star silver B&B and also provides extra touches such as homemade biscuits in each room. Most initial impressions are favourable. After settling in, hyperactive Annette has lined up her idea of fun for her guests: a cycling tour.

The group return to final host Annette's Hazelwood farm for one last meeting to discover how much they've been paid and to have the chance to defend their comments and their B&Bs, before the winner is revealed. After quite a few tissues, Annette gets down to announcing the winners and the losers.

Melvyn and Sindy kick-start the latest competition with their Morgan sports-car-themed B&B, The Pitstop, in Hertfordshire. Despite some good first impressions, Wayne and Deborah and Gill and Peter think the satin sheets are a bit of a stretch, and the absence of tea and coffee in the rooms and the presence of the odd cobweb also cause a raised eyebrow or two.

It's the turn of corporate couple Gill and Peter Tydie to host at the Victory at Mersea, their four-star B&B in Essex, which features 26 staff to organise a bar, restaurant, and accommodation. On a trip to a local fishery Wayne's behaviour once again proves irritating to some of the others, while Melvyn finds a hole in the bedsheets.

It's Dave 'Butterfly' Botha's turn to host his fellow B&B owners at his two-star establishment, Butterfly Paragliding B&B on the Isle of Wight. Tension builds from the outset as Wayne and Deborah discover that they will be spending the night in one of Dave's tepees in the garden, with an outdoor toilet. Dave's ace in the hole is paragliding lessons, which brings the group back together through the art of flight.

It's the turn of Deborah Morrison and Wayne Bingham to host at their B&B, Braddon Hall in Torquay. Melvyn and Sindy are curious to know if the B&B's chandelier's sturdy enough to do some swinging from, but find their four-poster bed a little squeaky. Gill and Pete are concerned over the mismatching type-faces in the in-room brochure, which is apparently a cardinal B&B sin.

The B&B owners gather for one last time - to find out how much they've been paid and reveal the winner. Melvyn and Sindy interrogate their guests over criticism on their feedback, Gill and Peter from the Victory bristle at the negative feedback and two underpayments, Butterfly Dave gets in a flap over a series of large underpayments, and Wayne and Deborah's payments leave the competition result in the balance.

Simon White and friend and neighbour Shirley Boyle are first to host at The Old Hall Country House in the picturesque village of Madeley in Cheshire. On arrival most of the guests are awed by the historical 16th century B&B. In the afternoon, Simon and Shirley take their guests tap dancing and in keeping with the five-star luxury to a private fine dining restaurant for dinner.

It's day two in the competition and the turn of cat-lover Eileen Finn to cater for her B&B competitors at the four-star Thornley House in Allendale, Northumbria. After being blown away by first hosts Simon and Shirley at the luxury Old Hall Country House, Eileen has her work cut out. Also, Eileen's beloved and very large Maine Coon cats are not to all of her guests' liking.

Jessica and Adrian Rashleigh are third to host at their three bedroom establishment Chy Conyn in St Ives, on the beautiful Cornish coast. The hosts hope that what they lack in size they will make up for in stunning surroundings. For the activity Jessica and Adrian take their guests on a magical mystery camper van tour of the local sights. At breakfast some of the guests struggle with the small breakfast room.

The final hosts are Tim and Karen from The Cavendish in Bournemouth. The guests are initially impressed with the 16-bed 'pink palace', but things go downhill when Simon and Shirley vigorously test their bed - and break it. Jessica and Adrian are worried that their room, situated right next to the front door, may mean a noisy night. Eileen however is delighted by the feline memorabilia left in her room as a special touch.

The rivals reconvene for one last time to find out how much they've been paid by their fellow B&B owners, and to sort out their differences. Simon White of Old Hall Country House is stunned by a generous overpayment, but Eileen Finn from the four-star Thornley is on the receiving end of some harsh criticism and some even harsher payments, and a shock underpayment leaves Tim from The Cavendish in Bournemouth reeling.

The first to host are husband-and-wife team Paul Billington and Flora Loizou from Silverwood Lodge in Cambridgeshire, the only couple in this week's competition. As the hosts show their three female guests to their rooms, Caroline, owner of The Dean Bed & Breakfast, gives a frosty response to the fact that they don't live on site, while Sue from Seashells Guesthouse is left in hysterics.

The group are off to Great Yarmouth to stay in Sue's dog friendly Seashells Guesthouse. After revealing that she allows dogs to sleep in the beds during the last B&B visit, no one knows quite what to expect. As soon as they pull up, all the guests are blown away by the doggy-themed exterior. The interior is equally memorable, with Paul and Flora finding themselves in the Cappuccino Room and Caroline in the Poppy Room.
In Bath, forthright American ex-banker Nancy Hampson isn't everybody's favourite person. There's trouble from the off for her at The Old Court Guesthouse.

The guests head to Scotland to stay with final host Caroline at The Dean Bed and Breakfast. The picturesque house, its two acres of gardens and breathtaking views across the Firth of Forth immediately win everyone over. However, rogue underwear in the drawers and cobwebs on the curtains are touches that the guests aren't so keen on.

It's the final day and the B&B hosts gather to find out how much they've been paid and who is taking the title of best value for money B&B. Galia faces some harsh feedback and questions the criticism over Slimmeria's rules and regulations. Tensions rise again between Galia and Ann and Bill, while Diane and Max from Ombersley feel stabbed in the back, especially by Ann and Bill's feedback, and are looking for some answers.
Steve and Beverly Green from Century Farm in North Devon greet their guests with a warm welcome before showing them around the farmhouse to examine their rooms.

The second visit of the competition is to the Little Gloster on the Isle of Wight, owned and run by 27-year-old professional chef Ben Cooke. Assisting him is his 81-year-old Danish grandmother Lilian, who has over 50 years' experience in the trade.

It's the third day of the week's competition and the turn of Stephen to host at the four-star Old Hall House. Stephen hasn't opened up to the group yet, much to the chagrin of some of the other guests, who seem to have taken a dislike to him.

The final visit of the competition is to the House of Agnes in Canterbury, run by ex-hotel inspector Sandie De Rougemont. With her guests now fully aware of her past career, could the bombshell backfire on the self-proclaimed 'B&B Buddha'?

There are tensions, tempers and tears as the group reconvene for one last time to thrash out the feedback, reveal the payments and announce the winner in the competition to be named best value B&B of the week. Paul and Flora from Silverwood Lodge are fired up about Nancy's comments and a tussle over TVs and hot water leads to accusations of lying and game playing.

The show returns as four sets of B&B owners take it in turns to host each other, before deciding which of their establishments provides the best value for money. The first B&B of the week is luxury weight-loss and detox retreat Slimmeria, owned by Galia and Michael Grainger. Health fanatic Galia's mission is to spread the Slimmeria message.

Jan and William Cheeseman have achieved a Five-Star Gold rating at 38 St Giles in Norwich, but the pursuit of perfection has been known to take its toll on this volatile pair. Things are anything but perfect for Galia when she arrives. Unhappy with her room due to the road noise, she asks to be moved. Luckily, a day on the racetrack gives Galia something to smile about as she has the ride of her life.

Fun-loving Ann and Bill host at their four-star B&B in Bude, North Cornwall. On arrival, Galia immediately complains about the lack of sea view, while Diane and Max query the luxury description of the premises. There's an indulgent Cornish cream tea, a Cornish stick dance, a drink in Ann and Bill's garden shed, and 'weekday caviar' for brekkie.

Hosts at Ombersley Bed & Breakfast are village bakers Diane and Max Seivewright. On arrival, Ann and Bill conduct a dust hunt in their room. Jan and William are left speechless by the outdated rooms, and Galia finds the journey across the hall for conveniences, inconvenient. Galia and Ann bicker over gluten-free bread and handwashing, and Ann is underwhelmed by her eggs at breakfast, and later she finds herself in tears.

It's the final day and all the B&B hosts gather for one last time to find out how much they've been paid. Watersedge hosts Alan and Sylvie kick things off, but ahead of discovering how much they've been paid, they're keen to question Tim and Amelia who complained about their room having no en suite.

The Pavilion is a London 'fashion and rock 'n' roll hotel', owned by former pop singer and Lamborghini lover, Danny Karne. His guests are wowed by the flashy sports car parked out the front and impressed by the colourful decor in the themed rooms, but some guests think they are all style, no substance.

The Fox and Duck in Therfield, Hertfordshire, is a country inn owned by John Luce and partner, Pat Sutton. John and Pat take their guests to the local golf club for a lesson in pitch and putt. The group appear to bond with lots of cheeky banter, and later they end the night with a sing-song.

The New Inn is in Newbridge-on-Wye and is run by Dave and Debbie Lang. As a keen pig breeder, Dave likes to get his guests in the mood for breakfast with quite a few piggy ornaments. As well as running a pub, he owns the on-site butcher's shop, and shows and also races pigs.

The final visit of the week is to Robert and Kerstin's establishment Westleigh Farm, in Somerset. Upon inspecting the rooms Danny finds dust and cobwebs and some wrong hangers, but there's praise elsewhere as Debbie comments on how big the showers are and John and Pat run some successful milk tests. Later, there's a beekeeping lesson and snooker, and some generous helpings for breakfast.

It's the final day and all the B&B hosts gather for one last time to find out how much they've been paid. Who will take the prize of the best value B&B? It falls to the ex-hotel inspector to award the prize.

Dan and Mardi Leonard welcome the others to their Brighton B&B, Guest and the City. The guests have mixed reactions to the contemporary décor and stained-glass windows. Alan and Jane think the room isn't user-friendly, Dubliner Phil is confused by the furniture, whilst Sarah and Jean-Pierre decry the lack of a shower curtain.

Phil Kiernan, entrepreneur and proud owner of the Farmer's Boy Inn in Gloucestershire, welcomes his guests and quickly introduces them to his latest business venture: pies. Alan and Jane take centre stage in a pie-making competition as their kitchen bickering entertains the group. Before breakfast the next morning the group work up an appetite on the bouncy castle.

Alan and Jane welcome their first ever guests to their brand-new purpose-built hotel boat, the Geanna. On arrival the guests enjoy the novelty factor, but Dan and Mardi think that space is too tight, while Jean-Pierre and Sarah are concerned about privacy. After inspecting their cabins, the Geanna embarks on her maiden voyage up the Thames.

Connoisseurs Sarah Langford and Jean-Pierre Kujawa have been running Sentry Mead, their 11-bedroom, five-star silver B&B for the past six years. Their guests arrive with high expectations, but Jane's high hopes are dashed by the mugs, Dan and Mardi don't like their shower mat, and Phil's not keen on the towels.

Una horda de zombis invade la granja y el grupo intenta escapar vivo entre el caos, pero no todos lo lograrán. Además, Rick se harta de las quejas del grupo y les da un ultimátum: si quieren que sea el líder, acatarán sus órdenes.

El grupo encuentra refugio en las instalaciones de una prisión federal abandonada tras meses en la carretera. Rick considera que se trata de un lugar seguro para que Lori pase los últimos meses de embarazo, pero quizá se haya equivocado.
Rick accede a dejar salir de sus celdas a los prisioneros si les ayudan a matar a los zombis que quedan en la prisión. Entretanto, la salud de Hershel empeora por momentos.

Andrea y Michonne descubren una comunidad de sobrevivientes liderada por un hombre llamado el Gobernador. Allá les ofrecen medicinas, comida, agua caliente y ropa limpia, pero Michonne desconfía del Gobernador y sus verdaderas intenciones.

En Woodbury, Michonne desconfía del Gobernador y planea irse sin Andrea. En la prisión, un sabotaje provoca que una horda de zombis penetre en la cárcel y, mientras Rick y sus compañeros los combaten, Lori entra en trabajo de parto.

Rick está totalmente abatido por la muerte de Lori, pero recibe una llamada telefónica sorprendente. Entretanto, Michonne ha descubierto el secreto del Gobernador y se dispone a abandonar Woodbury, a pesar de que Andrea quiere permanecer allá.

Michonne ve a Glenn y Maggie buscando provisiones, pero alguien más los observa: Merle, quien reconoce a Glenn como uno de los que le abandonó, a merced de los zombis, en una azotea de Atlanta. Entretanto, Rick sigue mentalmente inestable.
Michonne conduce a Rick, Daryl y Oscar a Woodbury para rescatar a Glenn y Maggie, a quienes el Gobernador está torturando para sonsacarles dónde se oculta el grupo de Rick.

El grupo de Rick invade Woodbury con la intención de rescatar a Glenn y Maggie. Michonne descubre el secreto familiar que oculta el Gobernador cuando trata de asesinarlo. En la prisión, un grupo desconocido atraviesa la verja de seguridad.
Rick y Maggie regresan a Woodbury para salvar a Daryl, quien está obligado a luchar contra su hermano. Entretanto, en la prisión, el grupo de Rick se encuentra con el grupo de Sasha y Tyreese.
En secreto, el Gobernador y sus hombres preparan una incursión mortal contra la prisión. Darryl y Merle llegan en mitad de la contienda.

El Gobernador permite a Andrea, acompañada de Milton, ir a la prisión a negociar la paz con su antiguo grupo. Mientras, Tyreese y Sasha llegan a Woodbury y le ofrecen al Gobernador información sobre la prisión a cambio de poder quedarse allá.
Rick, Michonne y Carl viajan al condado de Rick en busca de armamento y encuentran a alguien a quien creían muerto. Durante la misión, Rick cambia la percepción que tiene de Michonne.
Andrea concierta un encuentro entre Rick y el Gobernador para que negocien la paz, pero el Gobernador exige la cabeza de Michonne a cambio del alto el fuego.

Andrea descubre la verdad sobre el Gobernador e intenta huir para alertar al grupo de Rick, pero el Gobernador envía a sus hombres en su busca. Entretanto, alguien ha provocado un sabotaje en Woodbury y los sospechosos son Tyreese y Milton.
Rick duda entre entregarle o no a Michonne al Gobernador y poner así fin a la contienda. Sin embargo, Merle se anticipa a las órdenes de Rick y decide tomar una decisión por su propia cuenta.
El Gobernador y sus hombres lanzan un ataque contra la prisión, pero el grupo de Rick se defiende. Al final de la contienda, solo una de las dos comunidades podrá seguir existiendo.

Ambitious young radio producer Marcia Jeffries (Patricia Neal) finds a charming rogue named Larry "Lonesome" Rhodes (Andy Griffith) in an Arkansas drunk tank and puts him on the air. Soon, Rhodes' local popularity gets him an appearance on television in Memphis, which he parlays into national network stardom that he uses to endorse a presidential candidate for personal gain. But the increasingly petulant star's ego, arrogance and womanizing threaten his rise to the top.

After World War I, friends Eddie (James Cagney), George (Humphrey Bogart) and Lloyd (Jeffrey Lynn) return to America with ambitions for the future. Lloyd becomes a lawyer, but Eddie can only find work as a cab driver and eventually falls into the bootlegging business. Eddie and George become partners in crime, but the stock market crash destroys their operation and turns the old friends against each other, while Eddie falls in love with Lloyd's girlfriend, Jean (Priscilla Lane).

This biopic tells the story of how Samuel Clemens (Fredric March) became the renowned author Mark Twain. Growing up in the 1830s in Hannibal, Miss., Clemens works as a riverboat pilot on the Mississippi River. After he finds a picture of a beautiful girl (Alexis Smith) and vows to marry her, he quits his job and travels to Nevada in search of gold with his friend Steve (Alan Hale). In the midst of the Civil War, Clemens begins writing prolifically, thus beginning his famed career.

When life starts getting rough for Judge Hardy (Lewis Stone) and his family in their small town, they decide to move out west to aid their friends who have been caught in a dispute over water rights. The Hardy's have a hard time settling in to the new town when son Andy (Mickey Rooney) causes an accident that injures a child's horse and daughter Marian (Cecilia Parker) falls for an older man. The Hardys must now make amends, save their friends' ranch and save their own fortune as well.

The playboy lifestyle of Charlie (Fred Astaire) dismays his wealthy aunt (Marjorie Main). After he meets charity worker Angela (Vera-Ellen), Charlie genuinely falls in love with her, so much so that he actually floats in the air. When Charlie skips his own wedding to another woman (Gale Robbins), his aunt demands that he change his ways. Dedicated to winning over Angela, Charlie cleans up his act and even gets a job as a driver to impress her -- causing her to float, too.

In this sci-fi classic, a spacecraft travels to the distant planet Altair IV to discover the fate of a group of scientists sent there decades earlier. When Commander John J. Adams and his crew arrive, they discover only two people: Dr. Morbius and his daughter, Altaira, who was born on the remote planet. Soon, Adams begins to uncover the mystery of what happened on Altair IV, and why Morbius and Altaira are the sole survivors.

Bull Meechum (Robert Duvall) is a great fighter pilot -- so great that he dubs himself "The Great Santini." While his take-no-prisoners attitude and willingness to fight has served him well in the military, he's unable to turn it off at home. Eventually his competitive nature and abusive behavior take their toll on his relationships with his wife (Blythe Danner) and his rebellious 18-year-old son (Michael O'Keefe) after a friendly father-and-son basketball game turns ugly.

With a screenplay penned by the author himself, Stanley Kubrick brings Vladimir Nabokov's controversial tale of forbidden love to the screen. Humbert Humbert (James Mason) is a European professor who relocates to an American suburb, renting a room from lonely widow Charlotte Haze (Shelley Winters). Humbert marries Charlotte, but only to nurture his obsession with her comely teenage daughter, Lolita (Sue Lyon). After Charlotte's sudden death, Humbert has Lolita all to himself -- or does he?

A woman dreams of a picture-perfect life but finds she's close to losing everything. Gorgeous Fanny Trellis appears to have her choice of men, and wealthy Job Skeffington is her pick. Fanny's marriage plans are to preserve her family's reputation, but her machinations are rendered meaningless when her brother Trippy is killed in World War I. For Fanny and Job, the following years will be colored by loss, longing and self-discovery.

Professional soldier Curry (Rod Taylor) is tapped to oversee a dangerous mission in the Congo. The leader of the region needs Curry to guard a train carrying valuables that is snaking through areas controlled by rebel forces. Teamed with a local named Ruffo (Jim Brown), Curry recruits two more men for the job -- a heavy-drinking doctor (Kenneth More) and a former Nazi (Peter Carsten) -- and the foursome work to protect the train from invading marauders.

A ruthless crook, Walker (Lee Marvin), is betrayed by his partner, Mal Reese (John Vernon), who leaves him for dead on Alcatraz Island. Having survived, Walker returns years later to get revenge. He gets his first lead when a mysterious man (Keenan Wynn) tells him that Reese is now part of a vast criminal organization and dating Walker's wife's sister, Chris (Angie Dickinson). But after contacting Chris, Walker discovers that in truth she loathes Reese and is willing to help him get justice.

Al Lewis (George Burns) and Willy Clark (Walter Matthau) are a pair of feuding vaudeville comedians (Lewis and Clark, naturally) who performed together for 47 years before finally calling it quits.
